Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the producer and agency licence renewal calendar and the CE credit-gap register for every jurisdiction the carrier writes in; escalates any lapse to the Producer Compliance Manager

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Japan: Insurance Business Act Art. 115, Art. 116 and Art. 117 re-read on the FSA e-Gov statute database each renewal cycle, together with the operative solicitor-registration provisions (Art. 276 registration, Art. 282 five-year registration renewal) and, for US jurisdictions, each state's producer renewal and CE regulation as summarised in the NAIC State Licensing Handbook

In-scope processes.value: Producer onboarding to licence renewal to CE credit verification to appointment continuation - covering resident and non-resident individual producers, agency/entity licences with their DRLP designation, and Japan solicitor registrations administered through the Life Insurance Association of Japan

In-scope systems.value: NIPR Gateway Licensing/Renewal transactions and the Producer Database (PDB) are the system of record for licence status; the renewal log and CE transcripts are mirrored into the agency/producer management system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Producer Licence Renewal and CE Monitoring Procedure - population build from PDB, per-state renewal window table, CE transcript pull, gap remediation via assigned courses, renewal submission and fee payment, lapse suspension of appointments and commissions

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance; re-approved every January and out of cycle on any state bulletin that changes a renewal period, CE hour count or ethics-credit requirement

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Renewal-cycle driven: most US individual licences renew biennially on the producer's birth month or issue anniversary with CE (typically 24 credits including 3 ethics per biennium) completed before expiry; agency licences renew on the state's fixed date; Japan solicitor registrations renew on the five-year Art. 282 cycle

Deadline reminders configured.value: Renewal log auto-alerts at T-120, T-90, T-60, T-30 and T-7 days before each licence expiry date, plus a CE shortfall alert at T-90 addressed to the producer and their Agency Relations Manager

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Renewal log, NIPR transaction confirmation numbers, dated PDB screen captures and state CE transcripts retained 7 years from licence termination in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any producer who solicited or wrote business while a licence or CE requirement was lapsed is logged as an exception carrying the affected policy list, the commission clawback amount and a remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every lapse remediation, reinstatement filing and commission clawback before the exception may be closed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All individual and agency licences with an expiry date inside the test period, plus every producer credited with new business in the period, extracted from PDB and reconciled to the agency/producer management system roster

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance for solicitation on a lapsed licence; CE completion evidenced before expiry on 100% of renewals; more than 2% of renewals filed inside 7 days of expiry escalates to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation runs on the renewal cycle; the test runs quarterly over licences expiring in that quarter and the next, with an annual 100% sweep of the whole licensed population each January

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Must sit outside Licensing Ops and must not have submitted any sampled renewal transaction

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly licence renewal test workpaper (PDB extract, sample selection with seed, re-performance captures, CE transcript copies, exception log) filed in the compliance evidence repository under Licensing/Renewals

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Renewal log export by state showing licence number, expiry, NIPR transaction id, CE completion date and appointment effective date, producible to a DOI market conduct examiner within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Producer Compliance Manager answers state licensing data calls and FSA solicitor-registration enquiries; Regulatory Counsel clears any self-report of unlicensed solicitation before it leaves the company

checklist.step: Build the licensed-population master list
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Reports and run a PDB Company Report for each writing company NAIC co-code to list every individual and agency licence attached to the carrier.
Export the report to CSV with licence number, resident state, non-resident states, lines of authority, issue date and expiry date.
Pull the active producer roster from the agency/producer management system and join on National Producer Number (NPN) so roster-only and PDB-only records are both visible.
Send the roster-only list to the Agency Relations Manager to confirm whether each producer is still contracted or should be terminated.
Save the joined file as the renewal-cycle population, dated, in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the population lists every NPN with licence numbers, lines of authority and expiry dates, reconciled to the contracted roster.

checklist.step: Load each jurisdiction's renewal window, fee and CE rule into the renewal calendar
actions: For each state in the population open the NIPR Gateway state licensing requirements page and record the renewal period (biennial/annual), the renewal window opening day, the fee and whether the state renews on birth month or issue anniversary.
Record the CE requirement per state: total credit hours, ethics hours, LTC or annuity-specific hours and the credit-reporting lag from the CE provider to the state.

For Japan-registered solicitors, record the Art. 282 five-year registration expiry and the Life Insurance Association of Japan continuing-education course cycle required to keep the registration current.
Enter each rule as a row in the renewal calendar with the source page captured to PDF and named state-renewal-rules-yyyy-mm-dd.pdf.
checklist.done: every jurisdiction in the population has a calendar row with renewal period, fee, CE hours and a dated source capture.

checklist.step: Arm the reminder schedule against every licence expiry
actions: Load each licence expiry date into the renewal log and generate T-120, T-90, T-60, T-30 and T-7 day tasks.
Address the T-90 and T-30 alerts to the producer's own email plus their Agency Relations Manager so distribution owns the chase.
Set a separate CE-shortfall alert at T-90 that fires only where credited hours are below the state requirement.
Test the schedule by forcing one alert to fire and confirming delivery before relying on it for the cycle.
checklist.done: every licence in the population carries a live five-point reminder chain plus a conditional CE-shortfall alert.

checklist.step: Pull the state CE transcripts and compute each producer's credit gap
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the PDB Attachment Warehouse and CE transcript view for each NPN, or the state's own CE portal where the state does not publish through PDB.
Record credited hours by category (general, ethics, annuity/best-interest, LTC) and the transcript pull date on the producer's renewal row.
Compute gap = state requirement minus credited hours for each category and flag any negative balance.
Discount any credit posted with a completion date after the licence expiry - late-posted credit does not cure the renewal.
Send the gap list to the Learning & Development Specialist for course assignment.
checklist.done: every renewal row shows credited hours by category, the transcript date and a computed gap per category.

checklist.step: Assign and chase the courses that close the CE gaps
actions: Enrol each flagged producer in state-approved CE courses matching the deficient category, using only providers listed on that state's approved-provider register.
Set the LMS due date 45 days before licence expiry to absorb the provider-to-state credit reporting lag.
Run a weekly LMS completion report and hand the still-outstanding names to the Agency Relations Manager for direct contact.
Attach each course completion certificate to the producer record in the agency/producer management system.
checklist.done: every producer with a gap has an assigned approved course, a due date 45 days before expiry, and a filed completion certificate.

checklist.step: Verify credits have actually posted to the state before filing the renewal
actions: Re-pull the PDB CE transcript at T-45 and compare posted hours to the LMS completion records.
Where the LMS shows completion but the state shows nothing, contact the CE provider with the course code and completion date and demand a re-transmission within 5 business days.
Hold the renewal filing for any producer still short - filing a renewal on unmet CE draws a state deficiency notice.
Record the verification date and the posted-hours figure on the renewal row.
checklist.done: posted state credit meets or exceeds the requirement for every producer cleared to renew, with the verification dated on the row.

checklist.step: Refresh the background and disclosure answers carried into the renewal application
actions: Ask each renewing producer to reconfirm the Uniform Application background questions (criminal, administrative action, financial, child support, tax) in writing.
Compare the answers to the administrative actions already showing on the PDB Regulatory Actions section and query any difference.
Where a new administrative action or conviction appears, route the file to Regulatory Counsel before the renewal is filed and check whether a 18 U.S.C. 1033 written consent is required.
Log the reconfirmation date and outcome on the renewal row.
checklist.done: every renewing producer has a dated background reconfirmation reconciled to PDB regulatory actions, with new items routed to counsel.

checklist.step: Renew the agency and entity licences and confirm the DRLP designation
actions: List every agency/entity licence held by the carrier's owned agencies and its designated responsible licensed producer (DRLP) per state.
Confirm each DRLP still holds an active individual licence with the matching lines of authority - a lapsed DRLP invalidates the entity licence.
In NIPR Gateway run Business Entity Renewal for each state, paying the state fee by the stored EFT account.
Where a DRLP has left the business, file the DRLP change transaction before the renewal, not after.
checklist.done: every entity licence is renewed with a currently licensed DRLP recorded for each state.

checklist.step: Execute the individual renewals through NIPR Gateway and pay the fees
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Licensing to Renewals, select the state and upload the batch renewal file for producers cleared on CE and background.
Confirm each transaction returns a NIPR transaction confirmation number and the state fee is debited from the funding account.
Record the confirmation number, submission date and fee on the renewal row.
Work the rejected transactions the same day - typical causes are name mismatch, missing CE, unpaid prior fee or an unresolved regulatory action.
Escalate any renewal still unfiled at T-7 to the Producer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: every cleared renewal has a NIPR confirmation number and fee record, and every rejection is either cured or escalated.

checklist.step: Confirm the renewed status back in the Producer Database
actions: Five business days after each submission, re-run the PDB Company Report and confirm the licence status reads Active with the new expiry date.
Capture the PDB record to PDF as the renewal evidence and attach it to the renewal row.
Chase any state still showing the old expiry with the state licensing division, quoting the NIPR transaction number.
Update the licence expiry field in the agency/producer management system so downstream appointment and commission logic reads the new date.
checklist.done: PDB shows an active licence with the new expiry for every renewal, captured as evidence and synced to the producer system.

checklist.step: Suspend selling authority the moment a licence lapses
actions: Run the daily expired-licence exception report from the renewal log.
Set the producer's status to Not in Good Standing, which blocks new-business submission in the policy administration platform and suspends commission payment in the billing/commission platform.
Notify the producer and their agency in writing that solicitation must stop that day and quote the state's licensing statute.
Reassign any in-flight applications to a licensed producer of record and document the reassignment.
checklist.done: every lapsed producer is blocked from new business and commission the same day, with written notice sent.

checklist.step: Remediate lapses and reinstate where the state allows it
actions: Determine the state's reinstatement window and penalty (commonly a 12-month late-renewal window with a penalty fee, after which re-examination is required).
File the reinstatement or new application through NIPR Gateway and pay the penalty fee.
Identify every application and policy written during the lapse period, quantify the commission paid and raise the clawback with the billing/commission platform owner.
Assess with Regulatory Counsel whether the state requires self-reporting of the unlicensed activity and file within the state's required window.
Sign off the remediation on the exception record.
checklist.done: each lapse has a reinstatement outcome, a quantified clawback, a self-report decision and a signed remediation record.

checklist.step: Reconcile non-resident licences to the home-state licence
actions: For each producer, list the resident licence and every non-resident licence with its lines of authority from PDB.
Flag any non-resident line of authority not supported by the resident licence - non-resident authority cannot exceed the home state's.
Flag any producer whose resident state has changed, which requires a new resident licence and conversion of the old one to non-resident within the state's window (commonly 30 days).
Send the flagged list to the Agency Relations Manager for producer contact and record the resolution.
checklist.done: no non-resident licence carries authority unsupported by the resident licence, and every residency change has a filed conversion.

checklist.step: Publish the renewal log and report the cycle result
actions: Produce the cycle renewal log showing, per producer: NPN, states, expiry, CE hours posted, renewal filing date, NIPR confirmation number and final status.
Compute the cycle metrics - on-time renewal rate, CE-driven late renewals, lapses and lapse days, business written during lapse.
Present the metrics to the Head of Compliance and the Head of Distribution at the quarterly distribution compliance meeting.
File the log and the meeting minute in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a complete renewal log with cycle metrics is filed and reported to Compliance and Distribution leadership.

checklist.step: Retain the renewal evidence for the full retention period
actions: Move the renewal log, PDB captures, NIPR confirmations and CE transcripts into the repository under Licensing/Renewals/<cycle year>.
Apply the 7-years-from-licence-termination retention label so records survive the producer leaving.
Confirm the repository index makes the records searchable by NPN, state and licence number.
Run a retrieval test on three random NPNs and record the retrieval time.
checklist.done: the cycle evidence is filed under a 7-year label and retrievable by NPN, state and licence number within the tested time.

testing.step: Build the independent population of licences and writing producers
actions: Run your own PDB Company Report for every writing company NAIC co-code rather than accepting the Licensing Ops extract.
Extract from the policy administration platform every new-business application in the period with its writing producer NPN and application signature date.
Union the two lists so producers who wrote business but hold no current licence record surface immediately.
Reconcile the count to the agency/producer management system roster and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: the population is independently extracted, unioned with writing activity and reconciled to the roster.

testing.step: Reconcile every renewal in the period to a PDB status change
actions: Match each renewal-log row to a PDB record showing an expiry date after the prior expiry.
Compare the renewal filing date to the prior expiry date and mark anything filed after expiry.
List renewal-log rows with no matching PDB status change as automatic exceptions.
List PDB renewals with no renewal-log row - these show the log is incomplete, not that the work was done.
testing.done: every renewal-log row ties to a PDB expiry change, and both directions of unmatched rows are listed as exceptions.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of producers who wrote business within 30 days either side of a licence expiry date.
Take 40 further renewals selected at random with a recorded seed, stratified so every state with more than 10 renewals contributes at least one row.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Note any population row deliberately excluded and why.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, stratified by state and covers all producers writing near an expiry date.

testing.step: Re-perform the CE sufficiency test in the state record
actions: For each sampled renewal open the PDB CE transcript (or the state CE portal) and read posted hours by category as at the renewal date.
Independently compare posted hours to that state's requirement (total, ethics, annuity/LTC) taken from the state's own regulation, not from the Licensing Ops calendar row.
Treat credit posted after the expiry date as not counting, and treat a shortfall as an exception even if the state renewed the licence.
Screenshot the transcript and the state requirement page into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled renewal has an independently computed CE sufficiency conclusion with both source screens captured.

testing.step: Trace each sampled renewal to its NIPR transaction and fee
actions: Look up the recorded NIPR transaction confirmation number in NIPR Gateway transaction history.
Confirm the transaction is for the same NPN, state, licence type and lines of authority as the renewal row.
Agree the fee charged to the funding-account debit in the general ledger.
Flag rows where the confirmation number is missing, belongs to another producer or does not exist.
testing.done: every sampled renewal traces to a real NIPR transaction for the same NPN with an agreed fee.

testing.step: Recompute the reminder and expiry date maths
actions: For 15 sampled rows recompute the expiry date from the state rule (birth month or issue anniversary, annual or biennial) and compare to the renewal log.
Recompute the T-120/90/60/30/7 alert dates and confirm the alerts actually fired in the renewal log audit trail.
Confirm the CE due date was set at least 45 days before expiry to absorb the credit-posting lag.
Any wrong expiry date is an exception even where the renewal happened to be filed on time.
testing.done: expiry dates and alert dates recompute correctly and the alert audit trail shows delivery for every sampled row.

testing.step: Test whether any business was solicited on a lapsed licence or appointment
actions: For every producer in the 100% stratum, list applications with a signature date between the prior expiry and the reinstatement date.
Confirm the licence status in PDB as at each application signature date, not as at today.
Quantify the premium and commission on any application written during a gap and trace the commission clawback to the billing/commission platform.
Escalate confirmed unlicensed solicitation to Regulatory Counsel the same day as a reportable breach, not as a test exception.
testing.done: no sampled application was signed during a licence gap, or each instance is quantified, clawed back and escalated to counsel.

testing.step: Verify the entity licences and DRLP designations
actions: List every owned-agency entity licence from PDB with its recorded DRLP per state.
Confirm each DRLP holds an active individual licence with lines of authority covering everything the entity is authorised to write.
Confirm any DRLP departure in the period was followed by a filed DRLP change transaction before the next renewal.
Flag any entity licence renewed while its DRLP was lapsed.
testing.done: every entity licence has an active, appropriately authorised DRLP for the whole period, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception carrying NPN, state, the specific failure and the business impact in premium and commission.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - population gap, CE lag, provider non-reporting, fee failure, DRLP gap, chase failure - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for lapsed-licence business, an owner for the self-report decision with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time renewal rate, the CE-shortfall rate and the lapsed-solicitation count and compare them to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who filed none of the sampled renewals, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any open lapsed-solicitation breaches to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, computed rates and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Tier the role or contract by regulatory exposure before any search is ordered
actions: Open the requisition in Greenhouse and read the job description for handling of premium or claim funds, underwriting authority, solicitation of insurance and access to policyholder data.
Assign a tier: Tier 1 (transacts insurance business - producers, claims adjusters, underwriters, cash handlers), Tier 2 (policyholder data access, no authority), Tier 3 (no insurance nexus).
Record on the requisition that Tier 1 and Tier 2 engage 18 U.S.C. 1033 because the person will be engaged in the business of insurance affecting interstate commerce.
Send the tiering to the Recruiter and HR Business Partner so the offer template names the screen as a condition precedent to the start date.
checklist.done: the requisition carries a documented tier, the 1033 applicability call and an offer template that gates the start date on clearance.

checklist.step: Capture a compliant disclosure and authorisation before ordering anything
actions: Send the standalone FCRA disclosure document and the separate written authorisation for a consumer report through DocuSign - the disclosure must contain nothing else, no liability waiver and no state-notice text on the same page.
Add the state-specific notices (California ICRAA, New York Article 23-A, Minnesota, Oklahoma copy-of-report election) as separate documents in the same envelope.
Confirm the envelope is completed and countersigned before the vendor order is raised; an order placed on an unsigned authorisation is void.
File the completed envelope against the candidate record.
checklist.done: a signed standalone disclosure, a separate authorisation and all state notices are on file with a timestamp preceding the vendor order.

checklist.step: Order the background searches matched to the tier
actions: Order for Tier 1: seven-year county criminal in every county of residence, federal district criminal, national criminal database, sex offender registry, SSN trace and address history, employment and licence verification, and OFAC/SDN screening.
Add a credit report only for roles with fiduciary or cash-handling duty and only in states that permit it, recording the permissible-purpose basis.

Order the state fingerprint-based criminal history where the licensing state requires it, booking the candidate through the state's approved vendor (for example IdentoGO) with the state's service code.
Record the order date, vendor reference and expected turnaround on the screening register.
checklist.done: the ordered search set matches the tier, credit checks are state-permitted with a recorded basis, and fingerprints are booked where the state requires them.

checklist.step: Search the regulatory and licensing records the vendor does not cover
actions: For producers, run a PDB Producer Report on the NPN and read the Regulatory Actions section for every state, including suspensions, revocations, fines and consent orders.
Check FINRA BrokerCheck for anyone selling variable annuities and record CRD number, disclosure events and current registration status.
Search the state insurance department enforcement pages and the NAIC Regulatory Information Retrieval System (RIRS) for actions not yet posted to PDB.

For Japan-registered solicitors, check the Art. 279 disqualification grounds - rescinded registration within five years, bankruptcy without rehabilitation, and imprisonment-level convictions - and record the conclusion.
Attach every search result with its run date to the candidate record.
checklist.done: regulatory action, BrokerCheck and Art. 279 disqualification searches are complete and dated for every Tier 1 candidate.

checklist.step: Adjudicate each returned record against the written matrix
actions: Open the adjudication matrix and record for each hit: offence, jurisdiction, disposition, conviction date, sentence and whether it involved dishonesty, breach of trust or a violation of 18 U.S.C. 1033.
Apply the individualised assessment factors - nature and gravity of the offence, time elapsed, and relationship to the duties of the role - and write the reasoning, not just the outcome.
Disregard arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records and records outside the state's lookback where the state restricts their use.
Record the outcome as Clear, Clear with conditions, Prohibited person - consent required, or Not eligible.
checklist.done: every returned record has a written individualised assessment and one of the four defined outcomes on the adjudication worksheet.

checklist.step: Make and document the 1033 prohibited-person determination
actions: Test each conviction against 18 U.S.C. 1033(e)(1): a felony involving dishonesty or breach of trust, or a felony under 1033 itself, bars the person from engaging in the business of insurance without written consent.
Read the actual judgment or certified disposition rather than the vendor summary before calling a felony a dishonesty offence.
Where the bar applies, write the determination with the statutory analysis, the offence elements relied on and the date, and hold the offer or appointment.
Brief the Head of Compliance and the hiring manager on the bar and the 1034 civil penalty exposure for the company if the person is engaged anyway.
checklist.done: each felony conviction carries a written, counsel-signed 1033 determination based on the certified disposition.

checklist.step: Apply for the state commissioner's written consent where the person is otherwise wanted
actions: Confirm which state has jurisdiction - the domiciliary state of the insurer or the state where the person will transact - and download that department's 1033 written consent application form.
Assemble the pack: application, certified court records, letters of reference, the applicant's written explanation, evidence of rehabilitation and the proposed role description.
File with the state insurance department and log the filing date, the department contact and the acknowledgement in the 1033 consent register.
Keep the person out of the business of insurance entirely until the written consent order is granted - a pending application is not consent.
On grant, file the consent order and record any conditions it imposes on the role.
checklist.done: a filed consent application with a granted or refused order is on the register, and no barred person worked while it was pending.

checklist.step: Run the pre-adverse action sequence before any decline
actions: Send the pre-adverse action notice with a copy of the consumer report and the CFPB Summary of Your Rights Under the FCRA.
Hold the decision for at least 5 business days so the candidate can dispute inaccuracies with the vendor, and log the date the clock started.
If the candidate disputes, pause and reopen the adjudication on the corrected report before deciding.
Send the final adverse action notice naming the vendor, stating the vendor did not make the decision, and repeating the dispute rights.
File both notices with their send dates against the candidate record.
checklist.done: both notices are filed with at least 5 business days between them and any dispute is reflected in a reopened adjudication.

checklist.step: Gate the start date and the appointment on the clearance record
actions: Set the HRIS onboarding task Background screen cleared as a hard prerequisite for system access, payroll activation and the start date.
For producers, block the NIPR appointment transaction in the agency/producer management system until the screen clearance flag is set.
Where the business insists on an early start, require a written exception approved by the Head of Compliance naming the duties withheld until clearance.
Record the clearance date and the start or appointment date side by side on the screening register.
checklist.done: no start date or appointment effective date precedes the recorded clearance date without a written Head of Compliance exception.

checklist.step: Collect the Uniform Application background answers from producers and test them
actions: Obtain the producer's answers to the Uniform Application background questions on criminal history, administrative actions, unpaid judgments and tax obligations.
Compare each answer to the PDB regulatory actions, the criminal search and the court records already on file.
Treat a false or omitted answer as a separate integrity issue and escalate it independently of the underlying record.
Record the reconciliation and any discrepancy on the producer file.
checklist.done: every producer's background answers are reconciled to the independent searches with discrepancies escalated separately.

checklist.step: Screen against sanctions and financial-crime lists before engagement
actions: Screen the candidate or producer name and date of birth against OFAC SDN, consolidated sanctions, and PEP and adverse-media lists.
Adjudicate every hit to a true or false match with the identifiers relied on written down, not just a cleared flag.
Enrol the cleared name in ongoing rescreening so a later listing surfaces without waiting for the next hire cycle.
Escalate any true match to the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel the same day.
checklist.done: every engaged person has a dated sanctions and PEP adjudication and is enrolled in ongoing rescreening.

checklist.step: Maintain the 1033 consent register and rescreen on trigger events
actions: Keep a register of every prohibited-person determination, application filed, consent granted, its conditions and its expiry or review date.
Rescreen on trigger events: producer contract renewal, promotion into a Tier 1 role, a new administrative action posting to PDB, and any self-reported charge.
Require an annual written attestation from every Tier 1 employee and producer that nothing reportable has changed.
Chase non-returned attestations through the HR Business Partner and the Agency Relations Manager and record the closure.
checklist.done: the register is current, trigger-event rescreens are recorded, and every Tier 1 person has a returned annual attestation.

checklist.step: Protect the personal data collected by the screen
actions: Store vendor reports and court records in the restricted screening folder with access limited to the named Compliance and HR adjudicators.
Confirm the recruiting and HRIS records hold only the outcome flag and the clearance date, never the underlying criminal detail.
Run a quarterly access review of the restricted folder and remove anyone who has changed role.
Apply the deletion rule to candidates who were never engaged, per the retention schedule.
checklist.done: screening detail sits only in the restricted folder, access is reviewed quarterly, and non-engaged candidate files are deleted on schedule.

checklist.step: Handle post-engagement disclosures and departures
actions: Operate a duty for employees and producers to self-report any charge, conviction or administrative action within 30 days, stated in the code of conduct and the producer agreement.
On a self-report, suspend regulated duties pending a fresh 1033 determination by Regulatory Counsel.
Where the person must be removed, terminate the appointment through NIPR within the state's termination-notice window and state the reason code required by the state.
Record the outcome on the screening register and the exception tracker.
checklist.done: every post-engagement disclosure has a dated determination, a duty-suspension record and, where needed, a filed appointment termination.

checklist.step: Report the screening result set and retain the evidence
actions: Produce the quarterly screening summary - screens run by tier, clears, declines, prohibited-person determinations, consents filed and granted, and late clearances.
Present it to the Compliance Committee with the named exceptions and their remediation status.
File the summary, the register export and the committee minute under a 7-years-from-separation retention label.
Confirm the records are retrievable by name, NPN and requisition id.
checklist.done: a quarterly screening summary is reported to the Compliance Committee and filed under the 7-year label, retrievable by name and NPN.

testing.step: Build the population of everyone engaged in the period
actions: Extract from the HRIS every hire, rehire and internal move into a Tier 1 or Tier 2 role in the period with the effective start date.
Extract from NIPR Gateway every appointment transaction filed in the period with its effective date and NPN.
Add contingent workers and vendor staff with claims or cash-handling duties from the procurement system - these are routinely missed.
Reconcile the combined count to payroll starters and appointment counts, and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: the population covers employees, producers and contingent staff and is reconciled to payroll and appointment records.

testing.step: Reconcile every engagement to a screening register entry
actions: Match each population row to a screening register entry on name plus requisition id or NPN.
Compare the recorded clearance date to the start or appointment effective date and mark every row where clearance came later.
List population rows with no register entry at all as automatic exceptions.
List register entries with no population row to test whether the register is being padded with abandoned candidates.
testing.done: every engagement matches a register entry with a clearance date, and both unmatched directions are listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of Tier 1 engagements and 100% of everyone on the 1033 consent register.
Take 25 further Tier 2 engagements at random with a recorded seed.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Confirm the sample includes at least one contingent worker and one internal move if the population contains them.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all Tier 1 and all consent-register cases, and includes contingent and internal-move rows.

testing.step: Re-perform the adjudication on the raw vendor report
actions: Open the raw vendor report and court dispositions for each sampled record before reading the adjudication worksheet.
Reach your own conclusion against the published adjudication matrix, then compare it to the recorded outcome.
Treat right outcome, absent reasoning as an exception - the individualised assessment must be written down.
Capture the report page relied on into the workpaper with the personal data redacted to what supports the conclusion.
testing.done: each sampled record has an independent re-performed adjudication with the source page captured.

testing.step: Verify the FCRA disclosure, authorisation and adverse-action sequence
actions: Confirm the disclosure is a standalone document with no liability waiver or extraneous text and that the authorisation is separately signed.
Compare the authorisation signature timestamp to the vendor order timestamp - any order preceding signature is a fail.
For every decline, confirm the pre-adverse notice included the report and the CFPB summary of rights and that at least 5 business days elapsed before the final notice.
Recompute the business-day gap from the send timestamps rather than accepting the register field.
testing.done: disclosure form, signature sequencing and the recomputed adverse-action gap check out for every sampled decline.

testing.step: Test the 1033 determinations against the certified records
actions: Read the certified judgment for every felony in the sample and reach an independent view on whether it involves dishonesty or breach of trust.
Compare it to the recorded determination and treat any felony cleared without a written statutory analysis as a fail.
For each prohibited person, confirm a granted written consent order exists, name the issuing commissioner and check that the engagement date follows the order date.
Confirm no barred person performed regulated duties while an application was pending.
testing.done: every sampled felony carries a counsel-verified 1033 analysis and every prohibited person has a granted consent order pre-dating engagement.

testing.step: Trace producer screens to PDB regulatory actions and BrokerCheck
actions: Re-run the PDB Producer Report for each sampled NPN and read the Regulatory Actions section yourself.
Compare what PDB shows to the producer's Uniform Application answers and to the screening file.
Run BrokerCheck for variable-annuity producers and compare disclosure events to the file.
Flag any regulatory action that existed at appointment but does not appear in the screening file.
testing.done: PDB and BrokerCheck records for every sampled producer are reconciled to the screening file and the application answers.

testing.step: Recompute the gating dates and test the system controls
actions: For 20 sampled rows recompute days between clearance and start or appointment effective date and list every negative value.
Attempt, in a test environment, to activate system access on a record with the screen-cleared flag unset and confirm the control blocks it.
Confirm every early start has a written Head of Compliance exception naming the duties withheld.
Confirm the annual Tier 1 attestation return rate and list non-returners.
testing.done: the gating control is proven to block, every negative day-count has a written exception, and attestation non-returners are listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the person, role, tier, the specific failure and the duties performed while unscreened.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - tiering error, recruiter bypass, vendor delay, missing certified record, adverse-action sequencing, contingent-worker gap - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for a prohibited person engaged without consent, an immediate duty-suspension action and a counsel-led self-report decision.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where a bar applies, an immediate suspension action.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the late-clearance count, the missing-screen count and the prohibited-person-without-consent count against the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - with workpaper references for each finding.
Have the independent reviewer, who adjudicated none of the sampled screens, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any 1033 breaches to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the restricted-access workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, computed counts and a committee reporting date exists in the restricted repository folder.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly three-way reconciliation of the contracted producer roster, the carrier's appointment records and the state appointment records held in the NIPR Producer Database; escalates unappointed writers to the Producer Compliance Manager

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Japan: Insurance Business Act Art. 115, Art. 116 and Art. 117 carried as the regulation cites, applied through the provisions that actually govern appointment: Art. 276 and Art. 283 insurer responsibility for its registered solicitors in Japan, and each US state's appointment and termination statute plus the NAIC Producer Licensing Model Act appointment and 30-day termination-notice provisions

In-scope processes.value: Producer contracting to appointment filing to termination filing, reconciled quarterly across every writing company NAIC co-code and every state of appointment, including just-in-time appointment states where the first application triggers the appointment

In-scope systems.value: NIPR Gateway Appointments/Terminations and the Producer Database are the external system of record; the internal roster and appointment flags sit in the agency/producer management system and drive new-business acceptance in the policy administration platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Producer Appointment Reconciliation Procedure - PDB appointment extract by co-code, internal roster extract, three-way match on NPN plus state plus company, break classification into appointed-not-contracted, contracted-not-appointed and writing-without-appointment, and the cure or terminate decision

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Head of Distribution; re-approved annually and on any state bulletin changing appointment timing, just-in-time treatment or termination reason codes

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly reconciliation closing within 20 business days of quarter end; appointments filed within the state's window from the first application (commonly 15 days from application signature or the date the first policy is submitted); terminations filed within 30 days of the termination decision, with the for-cause notice to the producer required in most states within 15 days of the state filing

Deadline reminders configured.value: Reconciliation calendar tasks at quarter end plus 5, 10 and 20 business days; the agency/producer management system raises a daily alert on any application received from a producer with no appointment in that state, and a 30-day countdown on every recorded termination decision

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Quarterly reconciliation workbook, PDB appointment extracts, NIPR appointment and termination confirmations and break-resolution notes retained 7 years from the appointment end date in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every producer found writing in a state without an active appointment, every termination filed late and every appointment paid for on a producer no longer contracted is logged as a break with premium at risk, the cure filing date and the disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every break resolution, every backdated or late appointment filing and every for-cause termination reason code before the break is closed

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All active appointments per PDB by writing company and state at quarter end, the contracted roster from the agency/producer management system, and every new-business application written in the quarter with its producer NPN and state

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on business written without an active appointment in that state; 100% of terminations filed inside the state's 30-day window; unmatched breaks above 1% of the appointment population or any break older than one quarter escalates to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation reconciles quarterly; the independent test runs quarterly over the same quarter's reconciliation, with an annual full-population re-performance covering all states and co-codes

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Must sit outside Licensing Ops and Distribution Operations and must not have prepared or approved the reconciliation under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly appointment reconciliation test workpaper (independent PDB extract, three-way match output, sample with seed, NIPR confirmations, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Licensing/Appointments

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Appointment register by state and writing company with NPN, appointment effective date, termination date, reason code and NIPR confirmation numbers, reconcilable to the state's own records and producible to a DOI examiner within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Producer Compliance Manager answers state appointment data calls and appointment-fee invoices; Regulatory Counsel clears any self-report of unappointed production and any for-cause termination narrative before it is filed with the state

checklist.step: Extract the state appointment record from the Producer Database
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Reports and run the PDB Company Appointment Report for each writing company NAIC co-code as at quarter end.
Export to CSV with NPN, producer name, state, line of authority, appointment effective date, appointment status and any termination date.
Run the report separately per co-code - a producer appointed for the life company is not appointed for the P&C company.
Save the extract with its run timestamp as the external side of the reconciliation.
checklist.done: a dated PDB appointment extract exists per writing company co-code covering every state of appointment.

checklist.step: Extract the internal contracted roster and appointment flags
actions: Export every producer record with contract status, contract effective and termination dates, hierarchy/agency, states flagged as appointed and the internal appointment effective dates.
Include agency entity records and their affiliated individual producers so entity appointments reconcile too.
Include producers marked terminated in the quarter, since their appointments must have been filed as terminated as well.
Save the extract with its run timestamp as the internal side of the reconciliation.
checklist.done: the internal extract lists every producer and agency with contract status, appointed states and internal appointment dates.

checklist.step: Extract the production record so writing activity can be tested
actions: Extract every new-business application and issued policy in the quarter with the writing producer NPN, the state of the risk or residence, the application signature date and the policy effective date.
Include applications that were declined or withdrawn - solicitation without an appointment still counts in most states.
Add the split-commission and second-writing-agent records so producers behind the primary writer are visible.
Hand the extract to Licensing Ops with a record count and control total on premium.
checklist.done: the production extract covers applications, declines and split writers with NPN, state and signature date, with agreed control totals.

checklist.step: Run the three-way match on NPN, state and writing company
actions: Key every record on NPN + state + NAIC co-code and full-outer-join the PDB extract, the internal roster and the production extract.
Classify each break: appointed-not-contracted, contracted-not-appointed, writing-without-appointment, terminated-internally-but-still-appointed, and appointment line-of-authority mismatch.
Record the row counts per break class and the premium attached to the writing-without-appointment class.
Lock the matched workbook as the quarter's reconciliation baseline before any cures are filed.
checklist.done: every record falls into a matched row or a named break class, with counts and premium at risk recorded on a locked baseline.

checklist.step: Work the writing-without-appointment breaks first
actions: For each break confirm the state's rule - just-in-time states deem the appointment from the first application, whereas appointment-required states demand the appointment before solicitation.
Check the producer held an active licence in that state on the application signature date by reading PDB as at that date.
File the appointment immediately through NIPR Gateway Appointments with the correct line of authority and record the confirmation number.
Quantify the premium and commission written during the gap and refer the commission to the billing/commission platform owner for a clawback decision.
Escalate to Regulatory Counsel to decide whether the state requires a self-report.
checklist.done: every writing-without-appointment break has a filed appointment, quantified premium and commission, and a counsel self-report decision.

checklist.step: Clear the appointed-not-contracted breaks by terminating the appointment
actions: Confirm with the Agency Relations Manager that the producer genuinely has no live contract and no in-force block requiring servicing rights.
File the termination in NIPR Gateway Terminations with the state's required reason code, using a not-for-cause code unless a cause finding exists.
Record the termination effective date and confirmation number against the producer record.
Check the state's appointment-fee invoice so the company stops paying renewal appointment fees on dead appointments.
checklist.done: every appointed-not-contracted break has a filed termination with a reason code and the fee exposure stopped.

checklist.step: Clear the contracted-not-appointed breaks
actions: Confirm the producer holds an active licence in that state with a line of authority matching the products they are contracted to sell.
Decide with the Agency Relations Manager whether the producer will actually write in that state - do not appoint speculatively where the state charges per appointment.
Where the producer will write, file the appointment through NIPR Gateway and set the internal appointment flag from the confirmed effective date, not the request date.
Where the producer will not write, restrict the state on the contract so the policy administration platform blocks submissions.
checklist.done: each contracted-not-appointed break ends in a filed appointment or a state restriction on the contract.

checklist.step: File overdue terminations inside the statutory window
actions: List every producer whose contract terminated in the quarter and compute days from the termination decision date to today.
File the state termination through NIPR Gateway within 30 days of the decision, selecting the state's reason code and attaching the required narrative for a for-cause termination.
Send the producer the copy of the termination notice the state requires, typically within 15 days of the state filing, and record the send date.
Log any filing already outside the window as an exception rather than filing quietly and moving on.
checklist.done: every termination is filed inside the 30-day window with the producer notice sent, or the lateness is logged as an exception.

checklist.step: Get the for-cause reason codes and narratives cleared by counsel
actions: Review each proposed for-cause termination and the evidence behind it before the reason code is transmitted to the state.
Confirm the narrative states facts and dates only, since the statutory immunity for termination reporting depends on good-faith factual reporting.
Check whether the facts also trigger a separate state reporting duty for producer misconduct or a suspected fraud referral.
Sign off the code and narrative on the termination record before filing.
checklist.done: every for-cause termination carries a counsel-cleared reason code and factual narrative before it is filed.

checklist.step: Reconcile the appointment fee invoices to the appointment population
actions: Obtain the state appointment renewal invoices and the NIPR fee statements for the quarter.
Match invoiced appointments to the PDB appointment extract by NPN and state and list invoiced appointments that no longer exist internally.
Post the reconciled charge to the licensing cost centre and raise a dispute with the state for any invoiced appointment already terminated.
Report the recurring overpayment amount to the Producer Compliance Manager so terminations are prioritised.
checklist.done: appointment fees are matched to live appointments, with disputes raised and the overpayment quantified.

checklist.step: Confirm line-of-authority alignment on every appointment
actions: Compare the appointment line of authority in PDB to the products the producer is contracted to sell and to the products they actually wrote in the quarter.
Flag anyone writing variable annuities without a variable line of authority and an active FINRA registration.
Flag anyone writing long-term care or annuity products without the state's product-specific training on file.
File the additional appointment line or restrict the product on the contract, then record which route was taken.
checklist.done: every producer's appointment lines cover the products written, or the product is restricted on the contract.

checklist.step: Verify the cures actually landed in the state record
actions: Five business days after each cure filing, re-run the PDB Company Appointment Report and confirm the appointment or termination now shows with the expected effective date.
Capture the PDB record to PDF as the cure evidence and attach it to the break row.
Chase any state still not reflecting the transaction, quoting the NIPR confirmation number.
Update the internal appointment flag only from the confirmed PDB effective date.
checklist.done: every cure is confirmed in PDB with a captured record and the internal flag updated from the confirmed date.

checklist.step: Set the preventive controls so the same breaks do not recur
actions: Turn on the hard block that rejects a new-business submission where the writing NPN has no active appointment for that state and co-code.
Add the daily alert on any application received from an unappointed producer, routed to Licensing Ops and the Agency Relations Manager.
Wire the contract-termination event to auto-create the NIPR termination task with a 30-day countdown.
Test each control with a deliberate negative case and record the result.
checklist.done: the submission block, unappointed-application alert and 30-day termination task all exist and are proven by a tested negative case.

checklist.step: Report the reconciliation result to Compliance and Distribution
actions: Produce the quarterly reconciliation summary: appointment population by state, break counts by class, premium written without appointment, cures filed and terminations filed late.
Show the ageing of any break not cleared within the quarter and name its owner.
Present to the Head of Compliance and Head of Distribution within 20 business days of quarter end.
File the summary, the locked baseline workbook and the meeting minute.
checklist.done: a reconciliation summary with break ageing is reported within 20 business days of quarter end and filed.

checklist.step: Retain the reconciliation evidence
actions: File the PDB extracts, internal extracts, matched workbook, NIPR confirmations and break-resolution notes under Licensing/Appointments/<quarter>.
Apply the 7-years-from-appointment-end retention label.
Confirm the index makes records searchable by NPN, state, co-code and NIPR confirmation number.
Run a retrieval test on three random breaks and record the retrieval time.
checklist.done: the quarter's reconciliation evidence is filed under the 7-year label and retrievable by NPN, state and co-code.

testing.step: Rebuild the appointment population independently
actions: Run your own PDB Company Appointment Report per writing company co-code as at quarter end rather than using the Licensing Ops extract.
Compare your record count and state coverage to the extract used in the reconciliation and investigate any difference.
Pull the internal roster and the production extract directly from source systems with your own filters.
Agree the production extract premium control total to the statutory written premium by state before relying on it.
testing.done: an independently extracted population exists on all three sides with counts and premium agreed to source.

testing.step: Re-perform the three-way match
actions: Rebuild the full outer join on NPN + state + co-code from your own extracts.
Compare your break counts by class to the reconciliation's break counts and investigate every difference.
Check the reconciliation did not silently drop rows through inner joins, filtered co-codes or excluded declined applications.
Recompute the premium attached to the writing-without-appointment class.
testing.done: your break counts and premium at risk agree to the reconciliation, or every difference is explained in the workpaper.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of writing-without-appointment breaks and 100% of for-cause terminations.
Take 40 matched appointment rows at random with a recorded seed, stratified so every co-code and each of the ten largest states contributes rows.
Take 20 terminations filed in the quarter at random for deadline testing.
Record seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all writing-without-appointment and for-cause rows, and spans co-codes and major states.

testing.step: Verify each sampled appointment in the state record
actions: Look up each sampled NPN in PDB and confirm the appointment exists for the right co-code, state and line of authority.
Compare the PDB appointment effective date to the internal appointment flag date and flag any difference greater than zero days.
Confirm the producer's licence in that state was active on the appointment effective date.
Capture the PDB screen into the workpaper for each sampled row.
testing.done: every sampled appointment is confirmed in PDB with matching effective date, co-code, line of authority and an active licence.

testing.step: Test whether business was written before the appointment took effect
actions: For each sampled producer, list the earliest application signature date in that state in the quarter.
Compare it to the PDB appointment effective date and to the state's just-in-time rule read from the state's own appointment statute.
Treat any application signed before the appointment in a non-just-in-time state as a breach, not a documentation exception.
Quantify the premium and commission on every such application and confirm the clawback was raised.
testing.done: no sampled application pre-dates its appointment in an appointment-required state, or the premium, commission and clawback are quantified.

testing.step: Recompute the termination deadline maths
actions: For each sampled termination recompute days from the internal termination decision date to the NIPR filing date and compare to the state's window, commonly 30 days.
Recompute days from the state filing to the producer notice send date against the state's requirement, commonly 15 days.
Use the decision date in the contract record, not the date Licensing Ops was told, when the two differ.
List every filing outside the window with the days late.
testing.done: termination and notice day-counts are recomputed from the contract decision date with every late filing listed.

testing.step: Test the for-cause reason codes and counsel clearance
actions: Read the evidence file behind each for-cause termination and confirm the facts support the reason code transmitted.
Confirm the narrative is factual and dated, with no characterisation that would fall outside the good-faith reporting immunity.
Confirm a dated counsel sign-off pre-dates the NIPR filing.
Check whether any facts also required a separate misconduct or fraud referral and whether that referral was made.
testing.done: every for-cause termination has supported facts, a counsel sign-off pre-dating the filing and any required referral evidenced.

testing.step: Prove the preventive controls actually block
actions: In a test environment, submit a new-business application under an NPN with no appointment for that state and confirm the submission is rejected.
Terminate a test contract and confirm the NIPR termination task is auto-created with a 30-day countdown.
Review the production alert log for the quarter and confirm each unappointed-application alert has a recorded resolution.
List any alert closed without a cure filing or a state restriction.
testing.done: the submission block and auto-termination task are proven by test cases and every production alert has an evidenced resolution.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with NPN, state, co-code, the specific failure and the premium and commission exposure.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - contract feed lag, co-code omission, just-in-time misreading, termination decision not notified, fee-driven appointment avoidance - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for unappointed production, a counsel-led self-report decision and a commission clawback owner.
Carry every open break into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date, exposure figure and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the break rate against the appointment population, the unappointed-production premium and the late-termination rate, and compare each to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither prepared nor approved the reconciliation, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any unappointed-production breaches to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, computed break and lateness rates and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Each procedure approved by its named business owner and countersigned by the Head of Compliance; the procedure set is tabled annually to the Board Risk and Compliance Committee, and any change to the statement of business procedures goes to the FSA under the Art. 123 change route before it takes effect

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual review of every procedure with the review due date set 12 months from the last approval; out-of-cycle review within 30 days of a statutory amendment, FSA supervisory guideline update, product launch or examination finding; FSA notification or approval of a basic-document change obtained before the changed practice goes live

Deadline reminders configured.value: Procedure library alerts the named owner at T-60 and T-30 days before the annual review due date and daily once overdue; the regulatory change feed raises a review task on the affected procedure within 2 business days of a published amendment

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Every superseded version with its approval record, review evidence, change rationale and staff communication retained 10 years from supersession so the procedure in force on any past date can be reproduced for an FSA or DOI examiner

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Procedures past their review due date, conduct processes operating with no written procedure, and any practice found to differ from the approved statement of business procedures are logged with the gap, the interim control and the remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every overdue-review remediation, every newly written procedure covering a previously undocumented conduct process and every alignment fix between practice and the filed basic documents

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full procedure inventory as at test date, joined to the conduct obligation register and to the Art. 4 basic documents on file with the FSA, so both procedures without an obligation and obligations without a procedure are visible

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of conduct obligations mapped to a current approved procedure; zero procedures more than 30 days past their annual review date; any practice materially inconsistent with the filed statement of business procedures is a single-instance fail escalated to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is an annual review; the test runs annually over the whole inventory ahead of the Board committee submission, with a quarterly overdue-review check between full tests

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Must not own or have drafted any procedure in the sample and must not report into Market Conduct Compliance

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual procedure governance test workpaper (inventory extract, obligation mapping, sample with seed, version-history evidence, walkthrough notes, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Governance/Procedures

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Procedure inventory with owner, approval date, version and obligation mapping, plus the ability to produce the exact version in force on any nominated past date, deliverable to an FSA on-site inspection or a DOI market conduct examiner within 5 business days

checklist.step: Rebuild the inventory of conduct processes the Act actually governs
actions: Open the obligation record for the Insurance Business Act and list every conduct obligation it carries - solicitation conduct, product explanation and disclosure, suitability, replacement, complaint handling, claims payment and policyholder notification.
Add the conduct requirements from the FSA Comprehensive Supervisory Guidelines chapters on solicitation management and customer protection.
For each obligation, name the business process that discharges it and the department that runs it.
Send the draft list to the Head of Compliance and each department head for confirmation that no process is missing.
checklist.done: a confirmed list exists of every conduct obligation with its owning process and department.

checklist.step: Map each obligation to a named written procedure
actions: Build the mapping table with columns obligation, citation, process, procedure name, procedure id, version, owner, last approval date and next review date.
Mark every obligation with no procedure as a documentation gap and every procedure with no obligation as a candidate for retirement.
Record where one procedure covers several obligations so a change to it triggers a multi-obligation review.
Publish the mapping table as the index page of the procedure library.
checklist.done: every conduct obligation shows either a mapped procedure with version and owner or a logged documentation gap.

checklist.step: Reconcile the procedure set to the basic documents filed with the FSA
actions: Retrieve the statement of business procedures, the general policy conditions and the statement of calculation methods attached to the licence application under Art. 4.

Read each filed document against the corresponding internal procedure and list every place where practice has moved beyond what was filed - new distribution channel, new solicitation script, changed premium collection method.
Flag each difference as either a permissible operating detail or a basic-document change requiring an Art. 123 filing to the FSA.
Record the conclusion and the citation relied on against each mapping row.
checklist.done: every difference between practice and the filed basic documents is classified and, where required, raised as an FSA change filing.

checklist.step: Write or rewrite the procedures that failed the gap test
actions: Draft to the house template: purpose, regulatory citation, scope by product and jurisdiction, roles and their authority limits, the step sequence, the records produced, the escalation path and the review cycle.
Interview the people actually performing the process and write what they do, then fix the gap against the obligation rather than documenting an aspiration.
Name the system screens and fields used at each step so the procedure is executable by a new joiner.
State the record retained at each step and where it is filed.
checklist.done: each gap has a drafted procedure written from observed practice, naming systems, records and authority limits.

checklist.step: Run the annual review of every in-force procedure
actions: Schedule each procedure's review 12 months from its last approval date and issue the review task to its named owner.
Require the owner to confirm in writing that the steps still match practice, the cited provisions are current, the systems named still exist and the authority limits are right.
Require a substantive review note - a re-approval with no evidence of reading is treated as no review.
Record review date, reviewer, outcome (no change / amended / withdrawn) and next review date.
checklist.done: every in-force procedure has a dated review with a substantive note and a recorded outcome.

checklist.step: Feed regulatory change into an out-of-cycle review
actions: Monitor the FSA website and e-Gov public comment pages, the JFSA supervisory guideline revisions and the relevant US state bulletins for amendments touching conduct obligations.
Within 2 business days of a published amendment, raise a review task on every procedure mapped to the affected obligation.
Record the amendment reference, its effective date and the compliance-by date on the task.
Escalate any amendment whose effective date falls inside the normal drafting lead time so resourcing is decided immediately.
checklist.done: every published amendment has procedure review tasks raised within 2 business days carrying the amendment reference and effective date.

checklist.step: Route each procedure through the approval chain
actions: Require the business owner's approval first, since they must be able to resource the steps described.
Countersign as Head of Compliance only after checking the cited provisions and the escalation path.
Refer any procedure touching policyholder disclosure or claims payment to Regulatory Counsel before countersignature.
Record both approvals with names and dates in the document properties, not in an email thread.
checklist.done: every published procedure carries a dated business-owner approval and a Compliance countersignature in the document record.

checklist.step: Publish under version control and withdraw the superseded edition
actions: Publish the approved version read-only with a version number, effective date and the obligation mapping on the cover page.
Move the superseded version to the archive with its own effective and supersession dates so the version in force on any past date can be reproduced.
Remove or redirect every stale copy on team sites, shared drives and intranet pages found by a title search.
Confirm the library index shows one and only one current version per procedure id.
checklist.done: exactly one current version is published per procedure, superseded versions are date-stamped in archive, and stale copies are removed.

checklist.step: Communicate the change to the people who must follow it
actions: Issue a change notice naming what changed, why, the effective date and what each affected role must now do differently.
Send it to the affected distribution lists agreed with each department head, not to an all-staff list.
Attach the change notice to the procedure record so the communication evidence sits with the version.
Track the notice open rate and chase departments where it is below the agreed level.
checklist.done: every published change has a targeted change notice filed against the version with a tracked distribution.

checklist.step: Train the affected roles and record completion
actions: Build a short module for any procedure change that alters a step a front-line role performs, especially solicitation, suitability and complaint handling.
Assign it to the affected roles with a due date inside 30 days of the effective date.
Run weekly completion reports and escalate non-completers to their department head.
File the completion report against the procedure version as training evidence.
checklist.done: every step-changing revision has an assigned module with a completion report filed against the version.

checklist.step: Walk the procedure to confirm it matches what people actually do
actions: Sit with a performer and follow one live case end to end against the written steps.
Note every step performed differently, every step skipped and every step the system no longer supports.
Decide with the procedure owner whether the procedure or the practice is wrong and raise the corresponding fix.
File the walkthrough note with the case reference against the procedure record.
checklist.done: each walked procedure has a dated note comparing written steps to observed practice with a raised fix for every difference.

checklist.step: Escalate overdue reviews and undocumented processes
actions: Run the overdue-review report monthly and raise an issue on anything more than 30 days past its due date.
Raise a separate issue for each conduct obligation still carrying no procedure, naming the interim control holding the risk.
Report the count and ageing to the Head of Compliance monthly and to the Board Risk and Compliance Committee quarterly.
Do not close an issue on the strength of a promised draft - closure requires a published approved version.
checklist.done: every overdue review and undocumented obligation has an open issue with an interim control and is reported on the monthly cycle.

checklist.step: File any change to the statement of business procedures with the FSA before it operates
actions: Prepare the change filing for the affected basic document with the current and proposed wording side by side and the reason for the change.
Confirm with Regulatory Counsel whether the change requires FSA approval or notification and file on that basis.
Hold the go-live of the changed practice until the approval or the notification acknowledgement is received, and record the date received.
Attach the filing and the acknowledgement to the procedure record and to the obligation record.
checklist.done: no changed practice operates before its basic-document change is approved or acknowledged, with both filed against the procedure.

checklist.step: Table the procedure set to the Board committee
actions: Prepare the annual paper: inventory size, review completion rate, gaps closed, gaps open with interim controls, and any practice-to-filing misalignment found.
Load the paper to the board portal for the Risk and Compliance Committee with the mapping table as an annex.
Record the committee's resolution and any directed action with an owner and date in the minutes.
Feed the directed actions back into the procedure library as tasks.
checklist.done: the annual procedure paper is tabled, minuted with directed actions, and those actions are loaded as library tasks.

checklist.step: Retain the full version history for the retention period
actions: Export the annual snapshot of the library - current versions, approval records, review notes and change notices - into the repository under Governance/Procedures/<year>.
Apply the 10-years-from-supersession retention label so a past-dated version can still be produced.
Test reproduction by nominating three past dates and retrieving the exact version in force on each.
Record the retrieval test result in the workpaper.
checklist.done: the annual snapshot is filed under a 10-year label and the version in force on three nominated past dates was successfully reproduced.

testing.step: Build the population of conduct obligations and procedures
actions: Extract the conduct obligations recorded against the Insurance Business Act with citation, owner and mapped procedure id.
Extract the full procedure inventory from the document library with version, owner, approval date and next review date.
Full-outer-join the two on procedure id so unmapped obligations and orphan procedures both surface.
Reconcile the obligation list to the Art. 4 basic documents on file and to the conduct chapters of the supervisory guidelines to test the list itself for completeness.
testing.done: a joined population exists showing unmapped obligations, orphan procedures, and a completeness check against the filed basic documents.

testing.step: Reconcile the mapping to the filed basic documents
actions: Read the statement of business procedures and general policy conditions as filed and list the practices they describe.
Confirm each described practice has a current mapped procedure and that no procedure describes a practice outside what was filed.
Check every difference identified in the year was either classified as an operating detail with reasoning or filed with the FSA under Art. 123.
Treat an unfiled material difference as a reportable breach rather than a test exception.
testing.done: the filed basic documents reconcile to the procedure set, with every difference either reasoned or filed.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of procedures covering solicitation, suitability, replacement, complaint handling and claims payment.
Take 15 further procedures at random with a recorded seed across the remaining inventory.
Take 100% of obligations flagged as having no mapped procedure.
Record seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all high-risk conduct procedures plus every unmapped obligation.

testing.step: Re-perform the review-currency test on each sampled procedure
actions: Read the document properties for the last approval date, the reviewer and the recorded review note.
Recompute the review due date as approval date plus 12 months and compare it to the library's next-review field.
Treat a re-approval carrying no substantive review note as not reviewed, regardless of the date stamp.
Capture the properties screen and the review note into the workpaper.
