testing.done: each sampled procedure has an independently recomputed review due date and a judgement on whether the review was substantive.

testing.step: Verify the approval chain on each sampled version
actions: Confirm a dated business-owner approval and a dated Compliance countersignature exist in the document record, not only in email.
Confirm the approval dates precede the published effective date.
For procedures touching disclosure or claims payment, confirm Regulatory Counsel review is evidenced before countersignature.
Flag any version published with a missing or post-dated approval.
testing.done: every sampled version has both approvals dated before its effective date, with counsel review where required.

testing.step: Walk two procedures against live cases
actions: Pick one solicitation or suitability procedure and one complaint or claims procedure from the sample.
Select three completed live cases for each and trace the actual records produced against the steps and records the procedure requires.
Interview the performer without the procedure in front of them and compare what they describe to what is written.
Record every step performed differently, skipped or unsupported by the named system.
testing.done: two procedures are walked against three live cases each with every deviation from the written steps recorded.

testing.step: Test the regulatory change feed drove the reviews it should have
actions: List independently the amendments to the Insurance Business Act and the FSA supervisory guidelines published in the period.
Confirm each raised a review task on every mapped procedure within 2 business days of publication.
Confirm the resulting procedure amendment took effect on or before the amendment's compliance-by date.
List amendments that produced no task - these show the feed, not the review, is broken.
testing.done: every published amendment in the period ties to a timely review task and an in-force procedure change by the compliance-by date.

testing.step: Prove the version history reproduces a past-dated procedure
actions: Nominate three past dates spread across the last three years and request the exact procedure version in force on each for two sampled procedures.
Confirm the retrieved version carries an effective date on or before, and a supersession date after, the nominated date.
Search team sites and shared drives for stale copies of the sampled procedures and list any found outside the library.
Record retrieval times against the 5 business day regulator commitment.
testing.done: past-dated versions are reproduced correctly within the committed time and any stale out-of-library copies are listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the procedure or obligation, the specific failure and the conduct risk it leaves uncontrolled.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - owner vacancy, review-in-name-only, change feed miss, unmapped obligation, practice drift, unfiled basic-document change - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, for practice drift beyond the filed basic documents, a counsel-led FSA filing decision.
Carry every open exception into the next test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where practice drifted from the filing, a counsel decision.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the obligation coverage rate, the on-time review rate and the count of practice-to-filing misalignments against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who owns and drafted none of the sampled procedures, sign the workpaper.
Report the result to the Board Risk and Compliance Committee alongside the annual procedure paper and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, computed coverage and review rates and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the Market Conduct Annual Statement submission for every state where written premium crosses the participation threshold, and owns the officer attestation pack; escalates data-quality blockers to the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Japan: Insurance Business Act Art. 4(2) basic documents, Art. 110 business report and related statements for each business year, and Art. 121 (with Art. 122) on the appointed actuary's opinion, re-read at each reporting cycle; for the MCAS submission itself the current NAIC MCAS Data Call and Definitions for each participating line and each state's MCAS participation bulletin are re-read before the data pull

In-scope processes.value: Annual market conduct data reporting for every reportable line the company writes - Life, Annuity (including Variable Annuities), Long-Term Care, Disability Income, Private Passenger Auto, Homeowners, Health and Other Health as applicable - covering underwriting, policy administration, claims, complaints, replacements and lawsuits for the prior calendar year

In-scope systems.value: MCAS is filed through the NAIC MCAS application on the iSite+ platform using the state-by-state blank; source data is assembled in the enterprise data warehouse from the policy administration platform, the claims platform and the complaint case system

Compliance procedure documented.value: MCAS Preparation and Filing Procedure - participation determination by state and line, data element mapping to the current Data Call and Definitions, extraction and validation, ratio reasonability review, officer attestation, submission and post-submission amendment handling

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Regulatory Reporting Manager and the Head of Compliance; re-approved each January once the NAIC publishes the new Data Call and Definitions, because element definitions change between data years

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual for the calendar data year ending 31 December: the Property/Casualty, Life, Annuity, Long-Term Care and Disability Income lines are due 30 April; the Health lines are due 30 June; a state may grant an extension only on request before the due date, and the participation threshold is generally 50,000 US dollars of direct written premium in the state for the line

Deadline reminders configured.value: Reporting calendar tasks at 15 January (participation determination), 15 February (data extract complete), 15 March (validation and ratio review complete), 10 April (officer attestation) and 25 April (submission), with daily alerts from 25 April to the 30 April due date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Submitted blanks per state and line, the NAIC submission confirmation, the data extract with its query and run date, validation and ratio workpapers and the signed officer attestation retained 7 years from filing in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missed state or line participations, submissions filed after the due date, elements filed as unknown or zero without support, and any amendment filed after submission are logged with the cause, the states affected and the corrective filing date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late or amended MCAS submission and every decision not to participate in a state, before the filing season closes

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All state and line combinations where direct written premium for the data year exceeded the participation threshold per the statutory Schedule T and state page, joined to the MCAS submissions actually filed and to the underlying policy, claim and complaint counts for the data year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of threshold-crossing state and line combinations filed by the due date; every reported element traceable to a source query within a 0.5% tolerance on counts and 1% on dollar amounts; any missed participation or any submission after the due date is a single-instance fail escalated to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual; the test runs annually in the window between the data extract freeze and the officer attestation, so exceptions can still be corrected before submission, with a post-submission confirmation check in May

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Must not sit in Regulatory Reporting and must not have prepared or mapped any element of the submission under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual MCAS test workpaper (participation reconciliation to Schedule T, element trace-backs, ratio recomputation, submission confirmations, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Reporting/MCAS/<data year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Submitted blank per state and line with the NAIC confirmation number, the data dictionary mapping each element to its source query, and the signed attestation - producible to a state MCAS analyst or market conduct examiner within 5 business days of request

Regulator response path.value: The Regulatory Reporting Manager answers MCAS data-quality follow-ups from state analysts through the NAIC MCAS application; the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager owns any resulting market conduct enquiry and Regulatory Counsel clears any restatement narrative

checklist.step: Determine participation by state and line from the statutory premium record
actions: Pull direct written premium by state and line for the data year from Schedule T and the state pages of the filed annual statement, per writing company NAIC co-code.
Compare each state and line figure to the participation threshold in the current MCAS Data Call and Definitions, normally 50,000 US dollars of direct written premium.
Read each participating state's MCAS bulletin for state-specific inclusions, since some states call lines the NAIC blank does not.
Produce the participation matrix - state by line by co-code - and have the Statutory Reporting Manager confirm the premium figures tie to the filed annual statement.
checklist.done: a participation matrix exists per state, line and co-code, with the premium figures tied to the filed annual statement.

checklist.step: Load the current year's Data Call and Definitions and re-map every element
actions: Download the current MCAS Data Call and Definitions for each participating line from the NAIC MCAS page and diff it against last year's version.
List every added, removed or redefined element and the interrogatories, and mark which ones break last year's extraction logic.
Update the data dictionary so each blank element points to a named source table, filter and calculation in the warehouse.
Circulate the changed-element list to the claims, policy administration and complaints data owners so their extracts are adjusted before the pull.
checklist.done: the data dictionary reflects the current year definitions with every changed element identified and communicated to the source owners.

checklist.step: Extract the policy and underwriting elements
actions: Run the policy extract for the data year by state and line: policies in force at year end, new business issued, applications received, declined and incomplete, and policies cancelled or non-renewed with reason.
Split annuity elements by contract type and by qualified versus non-qualified, and separate variable annuity contracts as the blank requires.
Capture replacement counts, free-look cancellations and surrenders within the periods the blank defines.
Save each query with its run timestamp and row count so any figure can be re-derived later.
checklist.done: policy and underwriting elements are extracted by state and line with saved queries, run timestamps and row counts.

checklist.step: Extract the claims elements and the ageing buckets
actions: Run the claims extract by state and line: claims open at the start of the year, received, closed with payment, closed without payment, and open at year end.
Bucket closed claims by days to final payment using the blank's buckets (commonly 0-30, 31-60, 61-90, 91-180, 181-365 and over 365 days) measured from the date of due proof of loss.
Extract claims closed without payment by reason and the count of claims reopened, since these drive analyst attention.
Reconcile total claims paid in the extract to the statutory claims paid by state before releasing the file.
checklist.done: claims elements are extracted with correct ageing buckets and total paid reconciled to the statutory state page.

checklist.step: Extract the complaint and lawsuit elements
actions: Extract complaints received in the data year, split between those received directly from the consumer and those received via a department of insurance.
Apply the blank's definition of a complaint rather than the internal definition, and document where they differ.
Extract lawsuits open at year start, opened, closed and closed with consideration for the consumer, per the blank's definitions.
Reconcile the department-of-insurance complaint count to the NAIC Complaints Database System record for the company and explain any difference.
checklist.done: complaint and lawsuit elements are extracted on the blank's definitions and the DOI complaint count is reconciled to the NAIC database.

checklist.step: Validate the assembled blank against the NAIC edit rules
actions: Load the assembled data into the MCAS application on iSite+ and run the built-in validations for each state and line.
Clear every hard edit before submission and write a documented explanation for each soft edit that will remain.
Check internal consistency the edits do not catch - claims closed cannot exceed claims open plus received, policies in force must roll forward from last year's filing.
Record the validation run date, the edit list and the disposition of each edit in the workpaper.
checklist.done: no hard edits remain, every soft edit carries a written explanation, and the roll-forward consistency checks pass.

checklist.step: Review the ratios for reasonability before anything is submitted
actions: Compute the ratios state analysts compute: claims closed without payment percentage, percentage of claims paid beyond 60 days, complaint ratio per 1,000 policies, replacement ratio and free-look or surrender rate.
Compare each ratio to the prior two data years for the same state and line and to the published NAIC MCAS industry benchmarks where available.
Investigate every ratio outside the prior-year range or well outside the benchmark - most such moves are data errors, not conduct events.
Where the move is genuine, prepare the explanatory narrative now, before a state analyst asks for it.
checklist.done: every ratio is compared to prior years and benchmarks, with outliers either corrected in the data or explained in a prepared narrative.

checklist.step: Answer the interrogatories with evidence, not memory
actions: Work through each line's interrogatories on distribution channels, use of third-party administrators, producer training and complaint handling.
Take each answer from a named source - the TPA register, the producer training completion report, the complaint procedure - and cite the source in the workpaper.
Have the answers on distribution and TPA use confirmed in writing by the Distribution Operations Manager and the Vendor Manager.
Do not carry last year's answers forward without re-confirming them.
checklist.done: every interrogatory answer is sourced, cited and confirmed by the accountable business owner for this data year.

checklist.step: Obtain the officer attestation
actions: Circulate the final blanks with the validation summary, ratio review and interrogatory sources to the attesting officer.
Confirm the attesting officer holds the title the state requires and is authorised on the company's NAIC contact record.
Have the attestation signed and dated before 10 April so there is time to resolve a refusal to sign.
File the signed attestation with the blank set in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: a dated attestation signed by an authorised officer sits with the final blank set before the submission window closes.

checklist.step: Submit each state and line through the NAIC MCAS application
actions: Log in to iSite+ and open the MCAS application under the company's NAIC group and co-code.
Upload or key each state and line blank and submit, taking the confirmation number and timestamp for each.
Submit the Property/Casualty, Life, Annuity, Long-Term Care and Disability Income lines by 30 April and the Health lines by 30 June.
Where a state cannot be met, request the extension in writing from that state before the due date and file the response - an extension requested after the due date is a late filing.
Record every confirmation number against the participation matrix row.
checklist.done: every participating state and line is submitted by its due date with a recorded confirmation number, or holds a pre-due-date extension.

checklist.step: Confirm receipt at state level and close the matrix
actions: Five business days after submission, re-open the MCAS application and confirm each state shows the filing as received for the correct data year and line.
Chase any state showing no filing, quoting the confirmation number and timestamp.
Mark each participation matrix row Submitted and confirmed, with the confirmation date.
Report any row still unconfirmed to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every submitted row shows as received in the MCAS application, with unconfirmed rows escalated.

checklist.step: Handle state analyst follow-ups and data-quality challenges
actions: Monitor the MCAS application messages and company email for state analyst queries on outlier ratios or edit explanations.
Answer with the underlying source query, the record counts and the ratio recomputation rather than a narrative alone.
Where a query reveals a genuine reporting error, prepare an amended filing rather than arguing the original.
Log every query, the response and the closure date on the participation matrix row.
checklist.done: every state query has a sourced response and a recorded closure, with genuine errors routed to an amendment.

checklist.step: File amendments and correct the underlying process
actions: Prepare the amended blank showing the corrected elements and the reason for the change.
Re-run the validations and the ratio review on the amended data before resubmitting through the MCAS application.
Obtain a fresh officer attestation on the amended figures.
Raise a tracker issue naming the source-system or mapping defect that caused the error and assign it to the source data owner with a fix date before the next data year.
checklist.done: each amendment is validated, re-attested and submitted, with the underlying data defect assigned an owner and a fix date.

checklist.step: Feed the MCAS result into the conduct monitoring cycle
actions: Publish the submitted ratios by state and line into the conduct metrics dashboard alongside the prior two years.
Highlight the states where the company sits in the worst quartile of the published MCAS benchmark for any ratio.
Open a conduct review on each highlighted state and line, since these drive state examination targeting.
Report the outcome to the Compliance Committee with the exam-risk assessment.
checklist.done: the submitted ratios are published to the conduct dashboard with a conduct review opened on every worst-quartile state and line.

checklist.step: Retain the filing evidence and the reproducibility pack
actions: File the submitted blanks, confirmations, extract queries with run timestamps, validation and ratio workpapers, interrogatory sources and the signed attestation under Reporting/MCAS/<data year>.
Apply the 7-years-from-filing retention label.
Test reproducibility by re-running one saved extract query and agreeing the row count to the filed figure.
Confirm the pack is retrievable by state, line, co-code and confirmation number.
checklist.done: the filing pack is retained under a 7-year label, retrievable by state and line, with one query re-run proving reproducibility.

testing.step: Rebuild the participation population from the statutory record
actions: Extract direct written premium by state and line for the data year straight from the filed annual statement Schedule T and state pages, per co-code.
Apply the current threshold from the Data Call and Definitions yourself to derive the state and line combinations that must be filed.
Compare your derived list to the participation matrix and to the submissions actually made, in both directions.
Confirm the premium figures agree to the filed annual statement rather than to a management report.
testing.done: an independently derived participation list exists, compared both ways to the matrix and to the filings made.

testing.step: Reconcile every required filing to a confirmed submission
actions: Match each derived state and line to a submission confirmation number in the MCAS application.
Compare the submission timestamp to the 30 April due date, and 30 June for the health lines.
Treat any missing filing or any submission after the due date without a pre-due-date extension as an automatic exception.
List submissions made for state and line combinations that were not required, since over-filing also signals a broken participation control.
testing.done: every required filing ties to a confirmed, on-time submission, with missing, late and unnecessary filings all listed.

testing.step: Draw and document the element sample
actions: Take 100% of the ratio-driving elements - claims closed without payment, claims paid beyond 60 days, complaints, replacements and lawsuits.
Take 25 further elements at random with a recorded seed across the remaining blank, weighted to elements whose definition changed this year.
Cover the five largest states by premium and at least one small state in the sample.
Record seed, population size, stratification and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all ratio-driving and changed-definition elements, and spans large and small states.

testing.step: Trace each sampled element back to source records
actions: Re-run the saved extract query for each sampled element and compare the row count to the figure reported on the blank.
Drill from the aggregate to ten individual records per element and open each in the policy administration platform or claims platform to confirm it belongs in the element.
Apply the 0.5% count and 1% dollar tolerance and treat anything outside it as an exception.
Capture the query, the run timestamp and the drill-down evidence into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled element re-derives within tolerance with ten records individually verified in the source system.

testing.step: Re-perform the definitional mapping against the current Data Call
actions: Read the current year definition for each sampled element directly from the NAIC Data Call and Definitions.
Compare it to the filter logic in the data dictionary and decide independently whether the logic implements the definition.
Pay particular attention to elements whose definition changed this year and to the days-to-payment measurement start date.
Treat right number, wrong definition as an exception - it will restate next year.
testing.done: each sampled element's extraction logic is independently confirmed to implement the current year definition.

testing.step: Recompute the ageing buckets and the published ratios
actions: Recompute days to final payment for 30 sampled closed claims from the due-proof-of-loss date to the payment date and re-bucket them.
Recompute the claims-closed-without-payment percentage, the percentage paid beyond 60 days and the complaint ratio per 1,000 policies from the traced figures.
Compare your ratios to the submitted ratios and to the prior two data years for the same state and line.
List any difference and determine whether the cause is bucketing logic, denominator choice or source data.
testing.done: recomputed buckets and ratios agree to the submitted figures or every difference has an identified cause.

testing.step: Verify the complaint data against the independent NAIC record
actions: Obtain the company's department-of-insurance complaint count for the data year from the NAIC Complaints Database System.
Compare it to the complaint element reported on the blank by state and investigate every difference greater than one complaint.
Test ten complaints in the case system against the blank's complaint definition, particularly the direct versus DOI split.
Treat systematic under-reporting of complaints as a reportable issue, not a rounding difference.
testing.done: the reported complaint counts reconcile to the NAIC complaints record by state with every difference explained.

testing.step: Verify the interrogatories and the officer attestation
actions: For each interrogatory answer, obtain the cited source document and confirm it supports the answer for this data year.
Confirm the TPA and distribution channel answers agree to the vendor register and the producer roster.
Confirm the attestation is signed and dated by an officer holding the required title and listed on the NAIC contact record, before the submission timestamp.
Flag any answer carried forward from the prior year without re-confirmation.
testing.done: every interrogatory answer is source-supported for this data year and the attestation pre-dates submission by an authorised officer.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the state, line, element and the size of the misstatement.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - participation threshold missed, definition change not implemented, source system gap, bucketing logic, complaint definition, late attestation - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where the blank is already submitted, an amendment decision with the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Carry every open exception into the next data year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and an amendment decision where the filing has already gone.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the participation completeness rate, the on-time submission rate and the count of elements outside tolerance against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared none of the submission, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any missed or late filings to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, computed completeness and timeliness rates and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly conduct metric pack, the benchmark set it is measured against and the threshold breach escalations; hands confirmed conduct deterioration to the Head of Compliance and the relevant business owner

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Japan: Insurance Business Act Art. 115, Art. 116 and Art. 117 carried as the regulation cites and re-read on the FSA e-Gov statute database each year, applied alongside the FSA Comprehensive Supervisory Guidelines customer-protection chapter and, for the US benchmark set, the published NAIC MCAS ratio benchmarks and the NAIC complaint index method

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly conduct measurement across solicitation and suitability, policy issue and free-look, replacement, premium collection, complaint handling and claims settlement, for every line written including Variable Annuities, cut by state or prefecture, product, distribution channel and producer

In-scope systems.value: Conduct metrics dashboard built on the enterprise data warehouse, sourced from the policy administration platform, the claims platform and the complaint case system, with benchmark tables loaded from the published NAIC MCAS ratios and the NAIC Complaints Database System

Compliance procedure documented.value: Conduct Metric Monitoring Procedure - the defined metric set with its formulae, the benchmark source and vintage, the amber and red threshold table, the quarterly production and review calendar, the breach investigation route and the reporting line to the Compliance Committee

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Risk Officer; thresholds re-approved annually each time new NAIC MCAS benchmark data is published, since a static threshold drifts against a moving industry

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly cycle: data cut at quarter end, dashboard published by quarter end plus 15 business days, breach investigations opened within 5 business days of publication, and the pack tabled at the Compliance Committee within 30 business days of quarter end; the annual threshold recalibration follows the NAIC benchmark publication

Deadline reminders configured.value: Dashboard scheduler alerts the metric owner at quarter end plus 5 and plus 12 business days if the refresh has not run; every red threshold breach auto-creates an investigation task with a 5 business day acknowledgement timer to the named business owner

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Quarterly metric pack, the underlying data extract with its query and run date, the benchmark table with its publication vintage, breach investigation notes and committee minutes retained 7 years from the reporting quarter in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every red threshold breach is logged with the state, product, channel and producer cut, the driver identified, the corrective action and the quarter by which the metric must return inside threshold; unrefreshed or broken metrics are logged separately as monitoring failures

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off the closure of every red breach, confirming the metric has returned inside threshold for two consecutive quarters or that the corrective action is complete and evidenced

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All four quarterly metric packs for the period, the underlying policy, claim and complaint populations behind each published metric, and the full breach log with its investigation and closure records

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Every defined metric produced and published within 15 business days of quarter end; every metric re-derivable within a 1% tolerance of the published figure; 100% of red breaches acknowledged within 5 business days and closed or re-forecast within two quarters; any breach silently closed without evidence is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is quarterly; the test runs semi-annually over the two intervening quarterly packs, with an annual review of the threshold recalibration against the newly published benchmarks

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Must not sit in Market Conduct Compliance and must not have built or maintained the dashboard or the metric definitions under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual conduct metric test workpaper (metric re-derivations, benchmark vintage checks, breach log trace, committee minute references, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Monitoring/Conduct Metrics

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Quarterly metric pack with definitions, benchmark source and vintage, trend by state and product, and the breach log with actions - producible to a market conduct examiner or the FSA as evidence of ongoing self-monitoring within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager presents the metric history in examinations and MCAS follow-ups; Regulatory Counsel clears any characterisation of an adverse trend before it is given to a regulator

checklist.step: Fix the metric set and write down each formula
actions: Define the metric set to match what regulators actually score: complaint ratio per 1,000 policies in force, DOI complaint index, claims closed without payment percentage, percentage of claims paid beyond 60 days, replacement ratio, free-look cancellation rate, surrender within 12 months rate, suitability rejection and override rate, and application NIGO rate.
For each metric write the exact numerator, denominator, measurement window and exclusions in the metric dictionary.
Align each definition to the MCAS Data Call and Definitions wording so the internal metric and the filed statistic cannot diverge.
Have each definition confirmed by the owning business - Claims for claim metrics, Distribution for suitability and replacement, Consumer Affairs for complaints.
checklist.done: every metric has a written numerator, denominator, window and exclusions, aligned to the MCAS definitions and confirmed by the owning business.

checklist.step: Load the external benchmarks with their vintage
actions: Download the published NAIC MCAS ratio benchmarks for each line and load the industry median and quartile values into the benchmark table.
Pull the company's complaint index and peer group position from the NAIC Consumer Information Source and the Complaints Database System.
Record the publication date and data year of every benchmark value, since a benchmark two data years stale will mislead the committee.
Add internal benchmarks where no published one exists - the company's own trailing eight-quarter mean and standard deviation.
checklist.done: the benchmark table holds an external or internal comparator for every metric with its publication date and data year recorded.

checklist.step: Set the amber and red thresholds and get them approved
actions: Set amber at the industry third quartile or the trailing mean plus one standard deviation, and red at the industry worst quartile or mean plus two standard deviations, per metric.
Set an absolute red floor where regulator attention is certain regardless of peers - for example any state complaint index above 2.0.
Take the threshold table to the Chief Risk Officer for approval and record the approval date.
Re-approve annually when new benchmark data publishes, and record what moved and why.
checklist.done: an approved threshold table exists per metric with amber, red and absolute floors, dated and tied to a benchmark vintage.

checklist.step: Build the quarterly data cut
actions: Run the metric queries at quarter end cutting by state or prefecture, product, distribution channel, agency and producer NPN.
Reconcile the policy in-force denominator to the policy administration platform in-force count and the claims counts to the claims platform, before any ratio is computed.
Freeze the cut with a run timestamp so the published figure cannot silently move when the warehouse reloads.
Record row counts and control totals in the workpaper alongside the queries.
checklist.done: a frozen, timestamped quarterly cut exists with denominators reconciled to the source systems and control totals recorded.

checklist.step: Publish the dashboard with trend and benchmark on the same view
actions: Publish each metric with the current quarter value, the trailing eight quarters, the benchmark line and the amber and red thresholds on one chart.
Add the cut-by filters for state, product, channel and producer so an aggregate that looks fine can be decomposed on the spot.
Show the denominator alongside every ratio so a small-denominator spike is visibly a small-denominator spike.
Schedule the refresh for quarter end plus 12 business days and alert the metric owner if it fails.
checklist.done: the dashboard shows value, trend, benchmark, thresholds and denominator per metric with working cut-by filters and a monitored refresh.

checklist.step: Decompose every amber and red metric before calling it a conduct problem
actions: For each breaching metric, filter to state, product, channel, agency and producer to find whether the movement is broad or concentrated.
Check the denominator first - a state with 200 policies in force will breach a complaint ratio on two complaints.
Check for a data cause: a system migration, a definition change, a backlog release or a reclassification of complaint types.
Write the decomposition finding on the breach record, naming whether the cause is data, mix or conduct.
checklist.done: every breaching metric has a written decomposition naming the cut where it concentrates and whether the cause is data, mix or conduct.

checklist.step: Investigate the confirmed conduct breaches at case level
actions: Pull 20 underlying cases for each conduct-caused breach - the actual complaints, the actual late-paid claims, the actual replacements.
Read the case files for a common pattern: one producer, one product feature, one script, one claims handler, one system defect.
Interview the front-line owner about what changed in the quarter before writing the conclusion.
Record the pattern, the affected policyholder population and the potential remediation exposure on the breach record.
checklist.done: each conduct-caused breach carries a case-level pattern finding with the affected population and remediation exposure quantified.

checklist.step: Run the complaint metrics against the regulator's own record
actions: Compare the internally counted DOI complaints for the quarter to the complaints recorded against the company in the NAIC Complaints Database System.
Investigate any complaint the regulator holds that the company did not log - an unlogged DOI complaint is a control failure in its own right.
Recompute the complaint index using the NAIC method - the company's share of complaints divided by its share of premium - and compare to the published index.
Record the reconciliation and the index on the quarterly pack.
checklist.done: internal DOI complaint counts reconcile to the NAIC record and the complaint index is recomputed on the NAIC method.

checklist.step: Test the producer-level cut for outlier solicitation behaviour
actions: Rank producers by replacement ratio, free-look cancellation rate, surrender within 12 months rate and complaints per 100 policies sold, with a minimum volume floor to exclude noise.
Take the top 5% on any measure into a named producer review with the Agency Relations Manager.
Pull the suitability files for 10 of that producer's sales and read the needs analysis against the product sold.
Escalate confirmed unsuitable-sales patterns to the Head of Compliance for a supervision or termination decision.
checklist.done: outlier producers are ranked above a volume floor, reviewed at file level, and confirmed patterns escalated for a supervision decision.

checklist.step: Open corrective actions with owners and target quarters
actions: Raise one issue per red breach naming the metric, the cut, the driver, the affected population and the exposure.
Assign the owner in the business that controls the driver, not in Compliance, and agree the corrective action in writing.
Set the target quarter by which the metric must return inside threshold and the interim milestone at the next quarter.
Require monthly progress updates on the issue between committee sittings.
checklist.done: every red breach has an issue with a business owner, an agreed action, a target quarter and monthly progress updates.

checklist.step: Report the pack to the Compliance Committee
actions: Table the quarterly pack within 30 business days of quarter end showing every metric against its threshold and benchmark with the trend.
Present the red breaches with their drivers, actions, owners and target quarters, and the ageing of anything carried from prior quarters.
Name the states where the company sits in the worst quartile, since these drive examination targeting.
Record the committee's directions with owners and dates in the minute.
checklist.done: the pack is tabled within 30 business days with breaches, drivers, owners and ageing, and directions minuted with owners and dates.

checklist.step: Close breaches only on evidence of sustained recovery
actions: Require the metric to sit inside threshold for two consecutive quarters, or the corrective action to be complete and independently evidenced, before closure.
Check the recovery is real - confirm the denominator has not been inflated and the definition has not been loosened.
Sign the closure on the breach record with the evidence reference.
Keep closed breaches on the pack for two further quarters as a watch item.
checklist.done: no breach is closed without two clean quarters or evidenced action completion, signed with an evidence reference.

checklist.step: Recalibrate the thresholds when new benchmarks publish
actions: On publication of new NAIC MCAS benchmark data, reload the benchmark table and recompute the amber and red thresholds.
Show the committee which thresholds tightened and which loosened and what that does to the current breach population.
Never loosen an absolute red floor to clear a breach - record any proposal to do so as an escalation.
Record the recalibration date, the benchmark vintage and the approval.
checklist.done: thresholds are recalibrated on the new benchmark vintage with the effect on the breach population shown and approved.

checklist.step: Keep the metric definitions and the MCAS filing aligned
actions: Each January, diff the new MCAS Data Call and Definitions against the internal metric dictionary.
Update any internal formula the NAIC has redefined and restate the trailing eight quarters on the new basis so the trend stays readable.
Flag on the dashboard every metric whose basis changed and the quarter from which it changed.
Record the restatement and its rationale in the metric dictionary.
checklist.done: internal metric definitions match the current MCAS definitions with trends restated and basis changes flagged on the dashboard.

checklist.step: Retain the quarterly packs and their evidence
actions: File each quarterly pack with its frozen data cut, queries, benchmark table vintage, breach records and committee minute under Monitoring/Conduct Metrics/<quarter>.
Apply the 7-years-from-quarter retention label.
Confirm the pack is retrievable by metric, state, product and quarter.
Re-run one archived query and agree the row count to the published figure as a reproducibility test.
checklist.done: each quarterly pack is filed under a 7-year label, retrievable by metric and quarter, with one query re-run proving reproducibility.

testing.step: Build the population of published metrics and breaches
actions: List every metric in the approved metric dictionary and every metric actually published in each quarterly pack in the period.
List every amber and red breach recorded in the period from the dashboard threshold logic, independently of the breach log.
Extract the breach log from the issue tracker with acknowledgement, action, owner, target quarter and closure dates.
Compare the dictionary, the published set and the breach log so unpublished metrics and unlogged breaches both surface.
testing.done: the population shows every defined, published and breaching metric with unpublished metrics and unlogged breaches identified.

testing.step: Reconcile the published metrics to the source populations
actions: Agree the in-force policy denominator on the pack to the policy administration platform in-force count at quarter end.
Agree the claims counts to the claims platform and the complaint counts to the case management system for the same quarter.
Investigate any denominator difference greater than 1%, since the denominator drives every ratio on the pack.
Confirm the frozen cut timestamp precedes the pack publication date.
testing.done: every denominator and count on the pack ties to source within 1% and the frozen cut pre-dates publication.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of red breaches and 100% of metrics whose definition changed in the period.
Take 12 further published metric-quarter combinations at random with a recorded seed, spread across both quarters under test.
Include at least one metric from each of claims, complaints, replacement and suitability.
Record seed, population size, stratification and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all red breaches and definition changes, and spans all four conduct domains.

testing.step: Re-derive each sampled metric from raw data
actions: Read the numerator, denominator, window and exclusions from the metric dictionary and write your own query rather than re-running theirs.
Compute the metric for the sampled quarter and cut and compare to the published figure against the 1% tolerance.
Where they differ, run their query too and identify whether the gap is filter logic, timing or an exclusion applied but not documented.
Capture both queries and both results into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled metric is independently re-derived within tolerance or the source of the difference is identified.

testing.step: Test the benchmark values and their vintage
actions: Trace each benchmark value in the table back to the published NAIC MCAS ratio release or the NAIC Consumer Information Source page.
Confirm the recorded data year matches the source and that no benchmark is more than two data years stale.
Recompute the complaint index on the NAIC method from the company's complaint and premium shares and compare to the published index.
Flag any internally derived benchmark used where a published one exists.
testing.done: every benchmark traces to its published source with a confirmed vintage, and the complaint index recomputes on the NAIC method.

testing.step: Re-perform the threshold logic and breach identification
actions: Apply the approved threshold table yourself to the re-derived metric values for every metric-quarter in the population.
List every breach you identify and compare it to the breaches the dashboard flagged and to the breach log.
Treat a metric that breached but was not flagged as a control failure in the monitoring, not a reporting delay.
Confirm no absolute red floor was moved during the period to clear a breach.
testing.done: independently identified breaches match the flagged and logged breaches, with any missed breach or moved floor listed.

testing.step: Test the breach investigations at case level
actions: For each sampled red breach, read the decomposition note and confirm it names the cut, the driver and whether the cause was data, mix or conduct.
Pull five of the underlying cases the investigation relied on and confirm they support the stated pattern.
Confirm a conduct-caused breach produced a quantified affected population and remediation exposure, not just a narrative.
Flag any breach closed as a data issue where the underlying cases show a genuine conduct pattern.
testing.done: each sampled breach investigation is supported by underlying cases and the data-versus-conduct conclusion is independently confirmed.

testing.step: Recompute the timeliness and closure discipline
actions: Recompute business days from quarter end to dashboard publication for each quarter against the 15 business day commitment.
Recompute business days from publication to breach acknowledgement against the 5 business day commitment.
For each closed breach, confirm two consecutive in-threshold quarters or evidenced action completion, and confirm the denominator was not inflated to achieve it.
Confirm the pack reached the Compliance Committee within 30 business days of quarter end from the minute date.
testing.done: publication, acknowledgement and committee timings are recomputed and every closure is evidenced against the stated rule.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the metric, quarter, cut and the specific failure.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - definition drift, denominator error, stale benchmark, missed breach flag, unsupported closure, late publication - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a missed breach hid a conduct pattern, an immediate case-level investigation.
Carry every open exception into the next test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, for missed breaches, an opened case-level investigation.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the metric re-derivation pass rate, the publication timeliness rate and the count of missed or unsupported breaches against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who built none of the metrics or dashboards, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any hidden conduct patterns to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, computed pass and timeliness rates and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Acts as the standing examination coordinator - owns the exam readiness file, the universe-file specifications, the document request response library and the single point of contact for examiners; escalates production failures to the Head of Compliance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Japan: Insurance Business Act Art. 115, Art. 116 and Art. 117 carried as the regulation cites, applied through the FSA on-site inspection powers over insurers and, for US examinations, each state's market conduct examination statute together with the current NAIC Market Regulation Handbook chapters on examination standards and the standardised data request

In-scope processes.value: Continuous examination readiness across every business area an examiner scores - company operations and management, complaint handling, marketing and sales, producer licensing, policyholder service, underwriting and rating, and claims - for all lines written including Variable Annuities, in every state of licence and for FSA on-site inspection in Japan

In-scope systems.value: Exam readiness file held in the evidence repository with the universe-file extract jobs scheduled against the enterprise data warehouse and the response library indexed to the Market Regulation Handbook standards

Compliance procedure documented.value: Market Conduct Examination Readiness Procedure - universe file specifications and refresh schedule, standard document request response library, examiner contact protocol, privileged material handling, sample-file production, data-call turnaround targets and the exam close-out route

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and countersigned by the General Counsel because it governs how material is produced to a regulator; re-approved annually and on any NAIC Market Regulation Handbook revision

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Continuous: universe files refreshed within 10 business days of each quarter end so no examination starts from a cold build; on a call letter, the pre-exam questionnaire is due on the date the examiner sets (commonly 30 days) and initial universe files commonly within 10 to 20 business days; each subsequent examiner request is worked to the date on the request, with a 5 business day internal target for acknowledgement

Deadline reminders configured.value: Quarterly refresh tasks at quarter end plus 5 and plus 10 business days; during an examination every logged examiner request carries an internal due date set two business days before the examiner's date, with daily alerts to the owner from three days out

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Universe files as produced with their extract queries and run dates, every examiner request and the exact response and attachments produced, the pre-exam questionnaire, the draft and final reports and the close-out correspondence retained 10 years from the exam close in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missed or late examiner deadlines, universe files that failed reconciliation to the source system, files produced incomplete and any material produced without the privilege review are each logged with the request reference, the impact on the examination and the corrective action

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late or corrected production to an examiner and every decision to withhold material on privilege grounds, after General Counsel review

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The quarterly universe files for the period with their source populations, plus every examiner or FSA request logged during any live examination in the period and the responses produced against them

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Universe files refreshed within 10 business days of every quarter end and reconciling to source within 0.5% on counts; 100% of examiner requests met by the examiner's due date; zero productions of privileged or out-of-scope personal data; any missed examiner deadline is a single-instance fail escalated to the Head of Compliance

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; the test runs semi-annually over the intervening quarterly refreshes, plus a mandatory post-examination test within 30 days of any exam close covering the full request log

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Must not sit in Market Conduct Compliance and must not have prepared any universe file or examiner response under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Exam readiness test workpaper (universe file reconciliations, refresh timing, request log trace, production completeness checks, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Examinations/Readiness

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The readiness file itself - current universe files by business area, the response library keyed to the Market Regulation Handbook standards, the procedure set and the prior exam history with remediation status - producible on a call letter within 10 business days

Regulator response path.value: The Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager is the sole examiner point of contact and no business area answers an examiner directly; General Counsel clears every privilege call and Regulatory Counsel clears every written position taken with the examiner

checklist.step: Specify the universe files an examiner will ask for
actions: Take the standardised data request layouts from the NAIC Market Regulation Handbook and list the universes: new business issued, applications declined and withdrawn, policies cancelled and non-renewed, in-force policies, claims paid, claims denied, claims closed without payment, complaints, lawsuits, producer appointments and terminations, and replacements.
For each universe record the required fields, the date basis (transaction date versus effective date) and the cut by state and line.
Agree each specification with the owning system team - policy administration for underwriting universes, claims for claim universes, Consumer Affairs for complaints.
Publish the specifications in the readiness file so a call letter does not start a design exercise.
checklist.done: every examiner universe has a published field-level specification with an agreed system owner and date basis.

checklist.step: Build and schedule the universe extract jobs
actions: Build one parameterised extract job per universe taking state, line and date range as parameters.
Schedule the jobs to run within 10 business days of each quarter end and write the output to the readiness folder with a run timestamp.
Include the record identifier an examiner will use to request a file - policy number, claim number, complaint number - in every layout.
Alert the Market Conduct / Consumer Compliance Manager on any job failure the same day.
checklist.done: parameterised extract jobs run on a quarterly schedule, write timestamped outputs and alert on failure.

checklist.step: Reconcile every universe to the system of record before it is trusted
actions: Agree new business and in-force counts to the policy administration platform, claim counts and paid amounts to the claims platform, and complaint counts to the case management system.
Agree the state split to the statutory state page written premium so no state is silently missing.
Investigate any difference above 0.5% on counts before the universe is filed as ready.
Record the reconciliation with figures and date in the readiness file next to the universe.
checklist.done: every universe carries a dated reconciliation to its system of record inside the 0.5% tolerance.

checklist.step: Assemble the response library against the examination standards
actions: List the Market Regulation Handbook standards for each business area and, against each one, the document that evidences it - the procedure, the training record, the control test, the metric pack.
Store a current copy of each evidencing document in the readiness file, not a link to a page that may change.
Mark any standard with no evidencing document as a readiness gap and assign it an owner.
Refresh the library each quarter alongside the universe refresh.
checklist.done: every examination standard maps to a stored current document or an owned readiness gap.

checklist.step: Keep the exam history and remediation status current
actions: Maintain a register of every market conduct examination, FSA inspection and targeted review in the last seven years with the state, period, scope and final report.
Record each finding, the corrective action, the completion date and the evidence reference - examiners open by asking what the last exam found.
Flag any prior finding whose remediation is incomplete, since a repeat finding is treated far more severely.
Attach the final reports and the close-out letters to the register.
checklist.done: the exam register covers seven years with every finding's remediation status evidenced and incomplete items flagged.

checklist.step: Pre-write the pre-exam questionnaire answers
actions: Take the standard pre-exam questionnaire topics - organisation and control, outsourced functions and TPAs, systems used, record retention, complaint handling, producer oversight, anti-fraud plan - and draft the answers now.
Source each answer from a named document and cite it, so the answer and the evidence are produced together.
Have each answer confirmed by the accountable business owner and dated.
Refresh the answers annually and immediately after any material organisational or system change.
checklist.done: a dated, source-cited questionnaire answer set exists, confirmed by the business owners and refreshed annually.

checklist.step: Stand up the examination response team on a call letter
actions: On receipt of the call letter, record the state, scope, examination period, lines and the examiner-in-charge, and diary every date the letter sets.
Name the single point of contact, the area leads for underwriting, claims, complaints and producer licensing, and the General Counsel contact for privilege.
Brief the team that no examiner communication happens outside the single point of contact and nothing is produced without logging.
Book the examiner workspace, the read-only system access and the confidentiality arrangements for on-site work.
checklist.done: a named response team, a diarised date set and a controlled examiner access arrangement exist within days of the call letter.

checklist.step: Run the request log as the spine of the examination
actions: Log every examiner request with its number, date received, exact wording, the examiner's due date and the internal due date set two business days earlier.
Assign an owner per request and record the status daily.
Log the response with what was produced, the file names, the page or record count and the production date.
Never let a request be answered outside the log, however informal the ask.
checklist.done: every examiner request and response is logged with wording, owner, both due dates and what was produced.

checklist.step: Produce sampled files complete and in one pass
actions: For each requested policy or claim number, assemble the complete file - application, underwriting notes, issued contract, delivery receipt, correspondence, claim notes, payment records and complaint correspondence.
Run the completeness checklist per file type before production; a file produced with a missing delivery receipt reads as a records-retention failing.
Produce in the format the examiner asked for, with an index listing every document in each file.
Record the production in the request log with the file inventory.
checklist.done: every sampled file is produced complete against its checklist, indexed, and recorded in the request log.

checklist.step: Review every production for privilege and personal data
actions: Review each production for attorney-client privileged material, work product and litigation reserve information before it leaves the company.
Decide and record whether to withhold, produce under the state's confidentiality provision, or produce with a limited waiver, and log the basis.
Confirm personal data beyond the examination scope is redacted or excluded, consistent with the privacy standard.
Sign the production release in the request log.
checklist.done: every production carries a recorded privilege decision and a personal-data check signed off before release.

checklist.step: Answer criticisms while the examination is still open
actions: Log each examiner criticism or preliminary finding with the standard cited, the files it rests on and the error rate the examiner computed.
Re-perform the examiner's test on the same files and confirm or challenge the error rate with your own evidence.
Where the criticism is right, say so, and produce the corrective action already underway.
Where it is wrong, respond in writing with the file references and the procedure in force at the time, cleared by Regulatory Counsel.
checklist.done: every criticism has a re-performed test, a written response cleared by counsel and a recorded position before the draft report.

checklist.step: Manage the on-site logistics and the examiner relationship
actions: Hold a standing weekly status call with the examiner-in-charge and circulate an agreed action list afterwards.
Track the examination budget and billed hours where the state bills the company, and query variances early.
Prepare and rehearse the business area interviews so the person interviewed knows the procedure, the controls and the metrics for their area.
Debrief internally after each interview and log any commitment made to the examiner.
checklist.done: a weekly examiner status rhythm exists with logged commitments, prepared interviewees and monitored examination billing.

checklist.step: Test readiness between examinations with a mock exam
actions: Once a year, issue a mock call letter using the Market Regulation Handbook standardised data request for one business area.
Require the universe files and 20 sampled complete files inside the same clock a real examiner would set.
Score the result on timeliness, universe reconciliation, file completeness and privilege handling.
Feed every failure into the readiness gap list with an owner and a date.
checklist.done: an annual mock exam has been run to real deadlines with a scored result and owned gaps.

checklist.step: Close out the examination and capture the lessons
actions: On the draft report, distribute it to the area leads and collect factual corrections with evidence references inside the state's response window, commonly 30 days.
File the company response cleared by Regulatory Counsel and record the state's disposition of each point.
Add every adopted finding to the exam register with a remediation owner and date, handing it to the remediation process.
Run a lessons-learned session and update the universe specifications, the response library and the questionnaire answers with what the examination exposed.
checklist.done: the draft report response is filed inside the window and every adopted finding is registered with an owner and feeds the readiness file update.

checklist.step: Retain the complete examination record
actions: File the call letter, questionnaire, universe files as produced with their queries, the full request log, every production, the draft and final report and the close-out letter under Examinations/<state>-<year>.
Apply the 10-years-from-close retention label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by state, examination year, request number and produced file name.
Restrict access to the privileged-material subfolder to General Counsel and named Compliance staff.
checklist.done: the complete examination record is filed under a 10-year label, retrievable by request number, with privileged material access-restricted.

testing.step: Build the population of universes and examiner requests
actions: List every universe specification in the readiness file and every quarterly refresh output produced in the period, with its run timestamp.
Extract the full examiner request log for any examination live in the period with received dates, due dates and production dates.
Obtain the call letters and the standardised data requests directly so the log can be tested for completeness against them.
Compare the specification list to the refresh outputs so universes that quietly stopped running surface.
testing.done: the population covers every specified universe, every refresh produced and every examiner request, tested against the call letters.

testing.step: Reconcile the universe files to the systems of record
actions: Independently count new business, in-force, claims and complaints for the same period and state cut and compare to the universe file counts.
Agree the state split to the statutory state page written premium.
Apply the 0.5% count tolerance and list every universe outside it.
Check the universe layouts still contain every field the current standardised data request asks for.
testing.done: every universe is independently reconciled within tolerance and its layout confirmed against the current data request.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of examiner requests where the production date is after the examiner due date, and 100% of privilege-withheld productions.
Take 25 further examiner requests at random with a recorded seed across the request log.
Take 20 files produced to the examiner at random for completeness testing.
Record seed, population size, stratification and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all late and privilege-withheld productions plus a random request and file sample.

testing.step: Recompute the refresh and response timing
actions: Recompute business days from each quarter end to the universe refresh run timestamp against the 10 business day commitment.
Recompute business days from each sampled request received date to the production date and compare to the examiner's due date.
Use the examiner's own dated request, not the log field, when the two differ.
List every missed examiner deadline with the days late and whether an extension was agreed in writing.
testing.done: refresh and response timings are recomputed from source dates with every missed deadline and its extension status listed.

testing.step: Test the completeness of produced files
actions: For each of the 20 sampled produced files, list the documents the completeness checklist requires for that file type.
Open the production as it was sent and confirm each required document is present and legible.
Independently pull the same policy or claim from the source system and look for documents that exist internally but were not produced.
Treat an omitted delivery receipt, suitability form or claim denial letter as a production failure, not a clerical miss.
testing.done: each sampled production is compared to both the checklist and the source system, with omissions listed.

testing.step: Re-perform an examiner test on a sampled criticism
actions: Take two examiner criticisms from the period with their cited standard and error rate.
Re-perform the examiner's test on the same file set and compute your own error rate.
Compare it to both the examiner's figure and the company's response figure and identify which is right.
Flag any company response that disputed a criticism without a re-performed test behind it.
testing.done: two criticisms are independently re-performed with a computed error rate and the company's response position assessed.

testing.step: Test the privilege and personal-data controls on production
actions: For each privilege-withheld item, confirm a dated General Counsel decision exists with a stated basis before the production date.
Sample five produced items and confirm no attorney-client or work-product material went out unreviewed.
Confirm out-of-scope personal data was redacted or excluded consistent with the privacy standard.
Flag any production released without a recorded privilege sign-off in the request log.
testing.done: every withholding has a dated basis, sampled productions carry no unreviewed privileged material, and unsigned releases are listed.

testing.step: Test the exam register and prior-finding remediation
actions: Compare the exam register to the final reports on file for the last seven years and list any examination missing from the register.
For 10 prior findings, confirm the recorded remediation is supported by evidence, not a status field.
Identify any current-period criticism that repeats a prior finding and confirm it was escalated as a repeat.
Confirm the mock exam was run in the period and its gaps have owners and dates.
testing.done: the register is complete against the reports, sampled remediations are evidenced, repeats are identified and the mock exam is evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the universe or request number and the specific failure.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - extract job failure, layout drift, source data gap, file assembly omission, privilege review bypass, deadline mismanagement - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where material was produced late or incomplete to an examiner, a corrected production and a written notification to the examiner cleared by counsel.
Carry every open exception into the next test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where production failed, a corrected production plan.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the refresh timeliness rate, the on-time examiner response rate, the file completeness rate and the universe reconciliation pass rate against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no universe file or examiner response, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any missed examiner deadlines to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, computed timeliness and completeness rates and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the corrective action plan register for every adopted examination or inspection finding, tracks each action to the date agreed with the regulator, and escalates slipping actions to the Head of Compliance before the regulator has to ask

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes - Japan: Insurance Business Act Art. 115, Art. 116 and Art. 117 carried as the regulation cites, applied alongside the FSA business improvement order and improvement-report regime that follows an on-site inspection, and for US examinations each state's examination statute governing the report adoption order and the corrective action it directs

In-scope processes.value: Post-examination remediation for every adopted finding from a state market conduct or financial examination, an FSA on-site inspection, a targeted review or a regulatory settlement agreement - covering procedure change, system change, staff retraining, policyholder restitution and the confirmatory retest

In-scope systems.value: Corrective action plans, milestones, owners and evidence held in the GRC platform with each action linked to the finding, the examination record in the compliance evidence repository and any restitution population in the policy administration platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Examination Finding Remediation Procedure - finding intake from the adoption order, root cause analysis, corrective action plan drafting and regulator agreement, milestone tracking, restitution calculation and payment, evidence pack assembly, confirmatory retest and formal closure with the regulator

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and countersigned by the General Counsel, since remediation commitments given to a regulator bind the company; re-approved annually and after any settlement agreement that imposes its own reporting terms

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Event-driven from the adoption order: the corrective action plan is normally due to the state within 30 days of report adoption, interim progress reports on the cadence the order or settlement sets (commonly quarterly), restitution paid within the period the order specifies, and the FSA business improvement report submitted by the date stated in the order with follow-up reports thereafter

Deadline reminders configured.value: Every action milestone in the GRC platform alerts its owner at T-30, T-14 and T-3 days and daily once overdue; the regulator-facing dates - plan submission, progress report, restitution completion - additionally alert the Head of Compliance and General Counsel from T-30

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Adoption order, corrective action plan as filed, regulator acceptance, milestone evidence, restitution calculation and payment file, confirmatory retest workpaper and the closure letter retained 10 years from closure in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Missed regulator-facing dates, actions closed without evidence, restitution paid short or late, and any finding whose confirmatory retest fails are logged with the finding reference, the regulator commitment breached and the recovery plan

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off the closure of every finding only on the confirmatory retest result and the completed restitution file, and signs every extension request before it goes to the regulator

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All findings adopted in any examination report, inspection order or settlement agreement in force during the period, with their corrective action plans, milestones, restitution populations and closure records

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of regulator-facing dates met or covered by an agreed written extension obtained before the date; zero findings closed without a passed confirmatory retest; restitution paid to 100% of the identified population with a documented reconciliation; any repeat of a prior finding is an automatic fail escalated to the Board Risk and Compliance Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; the test runs quarterly over all open findings and mandatorily within 30 days of any finding being closed, so closure evidence is tested while the trail is fresh

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Owns the independent opinion on remediation closure and must not have performed or supervised any remediation action under test

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly remediation test workpaper (finding population from the adoption orders, milestone timing recomputation, evidence sufficiency assessment, restitution reconciliation, retest re-performance, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Examinations/Remediation

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per finding: the corrective action plan as filed, the milestone evidence pack, the restitution reconciliation showing population, amount and payment date, and the confirmatory retest result - producible to the examining state or the FSA within 5 business days of a progress enquiry

Regulator response path.value: The Head of Compliance owns all remediation correspondence with the examining state or the FSA; General Counsel clears every plan, progress report and extension request, and Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of continuing non-compliance before it is sent

checklist.step: Take the findings off the adoption order and register them individually
actions: Read the final report and the state's adoption order, or the FSA business improvement order, and create one register entry per finding rather than one per report.
Record on each entry the standard or statute cited, the examiner's error rate and sample size, the period examined, the directed action and any date the order sets.
Distinguish directed corrective actions from recommendations, and register both, since a recommendation reappearing next exam becomes a finding.
Link each entry to the examination record in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: every finding and recommendation in the order has its own register entry with the citation, error rate, directed action and ordered date.

checklist.step: Establish the real root cause before designing any action
actions: Pull the files the examiner criticised and re-perform the test to confirm the error and understand how it arose.
Work the cause back through the chain - procedure silent, procedure wrong, system defect, training gap, capacity, incentive - and name the one that would have prevented it.
Test whether the cause is confined to the examined state and period or is present enterprise-wide, and quantify the wider population now.
Write the root cause statement on the register entry and have the business owner agree it in writing.
checklist.done: each finding carries an agreed root cause statement supported by re-performed file testing and a quantified enterprise-wide population.

checklist.step: Draft the corrective action plan with dated, evidenced milestones
actions: For each finding write the actions that address the root cause - procedure amendment, system change, control insertion, training, restitution - each with a named owner and a completion date.
Name for every milestone the evidence that will prove it, before it starts, so nothing is later closed on assertion.
Set the dates against real delivery capacity, including the system release calendar, rather than the date that reads best to the regulator.
Add the confirmatory retest as the final milestone on every plan, scheduled at least one full cycle after the fix goes live.
checklist.done: every finding has a plan whose actions address the stated root cause, each with an owner, a date, a named evidence artefact and a closing retest.

checklist.step: File the plan with the regulator inside the ordered window
actions: Have General Counsel clear the plan wording, since dates and commitments in it bind the company.
Submit to the examining department, normally within 30 days of report adoption, or to the FSA as the business improvement report by the date the order states.
