Record the submission date, the channel and the recipient, and chase the acceptance if none arrives inside 30 days.
Attach the accepted plan to every register entry it covers.
checklist.done: the plan is filed inside the ordered window with counsel clearance, and the acceptance is recorded against each finding.

checklist.step: Fix the procedure and the system, not just the sampled files
actions: Raise the procedure amendment through the procedure library so the change is versioned, approved and communicated.
Raise the system change with the acceptance criteria written from the finding - for example the field becomes mandatory, the letter auto-generates, the deadline clock starts on receipt.
Book the change into a named release and record the release id on the milestone.
Where the system fix is months away, insert an interim manual control with its own owner, checklist and evidence, and say so in the progress report.
checklist.done: each finding has a versioned procedure change and a booked system change with acceptance criteria, plus an evidenced interim control where needed.

checklist.step: Retrain the people who performed the failed step
actions: Build training from the actual failed files, showing what was done and what the standard required.
Assign it to every person in the role, not only those whose files were sampled, with a due date on the milestone.
Include a knowledge check and record the pass rate as the evidence artefact.
Escalate non-completers to their department head and hold the milestone open until the roster is complete.
checklist.done: the whole affected role population has completed role-specific training built from the failed files with a recorded pass rate.

checklist.step: Identify and quantify the policyholders owed restitution
actions: Build the affected population from the root cause definition across the full period the error existed, not just the examined period.
Compute per policyholder the amount owed - underpaid claim, overcharged premium, wrongly applied surrender charge - plus the interest rate the order or the state statute requires.
Reconcile the population count and total to the general ledger and have the Controller confirm the accrual.
Have the calculation methodology reviewed by the Appointed Actuary where reserves or policy values are involved.
checklist.done: a reconciled restitution population and amount exists with statutory interest, a GL accrual and actuarial review where values are affected.

checklist.step: Pay the restitution and evidence delivery
actions: Issue payment with an explanatory letter cleared by Regulatory Counsel stating what went wrong, the period, the amount and the interest.
Track returned mail and uncashed cheques and run address tracing on them; unpaid policyholders remain an open commitment.
Escheat genuinely unlocatable amounts under the state unclaimed property rules and document the escheatment.
Reconcile amounts paid, returned and escheated back to the calculated population and file the reconciliation.
checklist.done: every identified policyholder is paid, traced or escheated, with a reconciliation from calculated to paid and a letter cleared by counsel.

checklist.step: Track milestones weekly and force early escalation on slippage
actions: Run the milestone status report weekly and require a written reason and a recovery date for anything amber or red.
Escalate to the Head of Compliance the moment a regulator-facing date is at risk, not on the date itself.
Refuse status updates that assert progress without the named evidence artefact attached.
Report the open finding population, ageing and slippage to the Compliance Committee monthly.
checklist.done: milestones are reviewed weekly with evidence-backed status, and at-risk regulator dates are escalated before they pass.

checklist.step: Send the progress reports the order requires
actions: Diary each progress report date from the adoption order or the settlement agreement, commonly quarterly.
Report actual status against each committed milestone, including what has slipped and why - a report that hides slippage destroys credibility for the rest of the remediation.
Have General Counsel clear the report before it is sent and record the send date and recipient.
Where a date cannot be met, request the extension in writing before the date passes and file the regulator's response.
checklist.done: every ordered progress report is sent on time and cleared by counsel, with any extension requested in writing before the date passed.

checklist.step: Assemble the evidence pack per finding as work completes
actions: Collect against each milestone the named artefact - approved procedure version, release note and test result, training completion report, restitution reconciliation.
Reject any artefact that does not actually evidence the milestone, such as a meeting minute standing in for a system change.
Index the pack by finding reference so a regulator progress enquiry can be answered in one pull.
Keep the pack current as work completes rather than assembling it at closure.
checklist.done: each finding has an indexed evidence pack holding the named artefact for every completed milestone.

checklist.step: Run the confirmatory retest on post-fix activity
actions: Wait at least one full processing cycle after the fix goes live so the sample is genuinely post-fix.
Draw a fresh sample from post-fix transactions using the examiner's own test method and sample size.
Compute the error rate and compare it to the examiner's original rate and to the tolerance the order set.
Where the retest fails, reopen the finding and revisit the root cause - the fix addressed the wrong cause.
checklist.done: each finding has a post-fix retest on a fresh sample using the examiner's method, with a computed error rate against the ordered tolerance.

checklist.step: Close each finding formally, internally and with the regulator
actions: Close internally only on a passed confirmatory retest and a complete evidence pack, signing the closure on the register entry.
Where the order requires it, request written closure from the department or the FSA, attaching the evidence summary.
File the closure letter or acknowledgement against the register entry and the examination record.
Keep the finding visible on the Compliance Committee pack for two further quarters as a watch item.
checklist.done: each finding is closed on a passed retest and complete evidence, with the regulator's written closure filed where required.

checklist.step: Sweep the fix across states, products and channels the exam did not reach
actions: Test whether the same root cause exists in states, products, channels or entities outside the examined scope.
Extend the procedure change, system change and training to those populations and record the extension on the register entry.
Decide with Regulatory Counsel whether any other state must be notified or whether restitution is owed to its policyholders.
Record the enterprise-wide scope decision and its reasoning, since an examiner in the next state will ask.
checklist.done: each finding carries a documented enterprise-wide scope decision with the fix extended and any further-state notification decided by counsel.

checklist.step: Report to the Board and retain the remediation record
actions: Report to the Board Risk and Compliance Committee quarterly: open findings, ageing, regulator dates met and missed, restitution paid, retests passed and failed, and repeat findings.
Flag every repeat of a prior examination finding explicitly, since repeats drive penalties and settlement agreements.
File the adoption order, plan, evidence packs, restitution file, retest workpaper and closure letters under Examinations/Remediation/<exam> with a 10-years-from-closure label.
Confirm the record is retrievable by finding reference, state and examination year.
checklist.done: remediation status including repeats is reported quarterly to the Board committee and the full record is filed under a 10-year label.

testing.step: Build the finding population from the source orders
actions: Read every examination report, adoption order, FSA improvement order and settlement agreement in force during the period and list each finding and recommendation yourself.
Compare your list to the GRC register and list findings that never made it into the register.
Confirm each register entry carries the citation, error rate, directed action and the regulator-facing date from the order.
Include recommendations, since an unregistered recommendation becomes next exam's finding.
testing.done: an independently derived finding list is reconciled to the register with every unregistered finding or recommendation identified.

testing.step: Reconcile every finding to a plan filed inside the ordered window
actions: Match each finding to a corrective action plan and recompute days from the report adoption date to the plan submission date against the ordered window, normally 30 days.
Confirm General Counsel clearance is dated before the submission date.
Confirm the regulator's acceptance is on file or that the chase is evidenced where none arrived.
List findings with no plan, a late plan or no acceptance as automatic exceptions.
testing.done: every finding ties to a counsel-cleared plan filed inside the ordered window with acceptance or an evidenced chase.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of findings closed in the period, 100% of findings involving restitution and 100% of repeat findings.
Take 15 further open findings at random with a recorded seed across examinations and business areas.
Ensure the sample covers each examining state and any FSA order in force.
Record seed, population size, stratification and selection date.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all closed, restitution and repeat findings plus a random open-finding sample.

testing.step: Test the root cause analysis behind each sampled plan
actions: Read the root cause statement and confirm it is supported by re-performed file testing rather than assertion.
Check each planned action actually addresses the stated cause - training will not fix a system defect and a procedure edit will not fix a capacity problem.
Confirm the enterprise-wide population was quantified rather than the analysis stopping at the examined state and period.
Flag any plan whose actions could not prevent recurrence even if fully delivered.
testing.done: each sampled plan's root cause is evidence-supported and its actions are independently judged capable of preventing recurrence.

testing.step: Recompute every milestone and regulator-facing date
actions: Extract the milestone history with original dates, revised dates and completion dates for each sampled finding.
Recompute days late against the original committed date, not the last revised one, and list every regulator-facing date missed.
For each missed date, confirm a written extension was requested and granted before the date passed.
Count silent date revisions - a milestone moved without a regulator notification is an exception.
testing.done: lateness is recomputed against original commitments with every missed regulator date and silent revision listed.

testing.step: Test the sufficiency of the closure evidence
actions: For each closed milestone, open the named evidence artefact and judge whether it proves the milestone rather than describes it.

Confirm a procedure change has an approved version with an effective date, a system change has a release note and a passed test result, and training has a completion roster covering the whole role population.
Flag any milestone closed on a meeting minute, an email assertion or a status field.
Confirm the evidence pack is indexed by finding reference and retrievable in one pull.
testing.done: every sampled closed milestone is supported by an artefact that proves it, with assertion-only closures listed.

testing.step: Reconcile the restitution population, amount and payment
actions: Rebuild the affected population from the root cause definition over the full error period and compare the count to the remediation population.
Recompute the amount owed and the statutory interest for 20 policyholders and compare to the amounts paid.
Agree total paid, returned and escheated back to the calculated total and to the general ledger accrual.
List any policyholder in your population who received nothing, since an under-scoped population is the most common restitution failure.
testing.done: the restitution population, per-policyholder amounts, interest and total paid all reconcile, with any omitted policyholders listed.

testing.step: Re-perform the confirmatory retest
actions: Confirm the retest sample was drawn from transactions after the fix went live, allowing at least one full processing cycle.
Draw your own fresh post-fix sample using the examiner's method and sample size and compute your own error rate.
Compare your rate to the retest rate and to the tolerance the order set, and treat any finding closed on a failing or pre-fix retest as a fail.
Check whether the same error appears in states or products outside the examined scope, testing the enterprise-wide sweep.
testing.done: the retest is independently re-performed on a genuine post-fix sample with a computed error rate and the enterprise sweep tested.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the finding reference, the examination, the specific failure and the regulator commitment affected.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list - finding not registered, wrong root cause, unresourced milestone, evidence-free closure, under-scoped restitution, retest before fix - and an owner.
Set a remediation date and, where a regulator commitment was breached, a counsel-cleared notification to the regulator.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where a commitment was breached, a counsel-cleared regulator notification.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time regulator date rate, the evidenced-closure rate, the restitution completeness rate and the retest pass rate against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion - effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective - citing the workpaper references behind each figure.
Sign as the independent reviewer, having performed and supervised none of the remediation actions tested.
Report the result, every breached regulator commitment and every repeat finding to the Board Risk and Compliance Committee and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, computed rates and a Board committee reporting date exists in the repository.
